translations.literal: Volume Number One Hundred Fifty.
translations.idiomatic: Volume 150.

sentences.zh: 【梁紀六】　起閼逢執徐，盡旃蒙大荒落，凡二年。

translations.literal: [Liang Annals 6] From Yamou Zhixu through Zhanmeng Dahuangluo; two years in all.
translations.idiomatic: [Liang Annals 6] From Yamou Zhixu through Zhanmeng Dahuangluo—two years in all.

sentences.zh: 高祖武皇帝六普通五年（

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Putong of Emperor Wu the Gaozu (
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Putong of Emperor Wu (

sentences.zh: 甲辰，公元五二四年）

translations.literal: jiachen, the year 524 CE).
translations.idiomatic: jiachen, 524 CE).

sentences.zh: 春，正月，辛丑，魏主祀南郊。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on the day xinchou, the Wei ruler sacrificed at the Southern Suburbs.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on the day xinchou, the Wei emperor offered sacrifice at the Southern Suburbs.

sentences.zh: 三月，魏以臨淮王彧都督北討諸軍事，討破六韓拔陵。

translations.literal: In the third month, Wei appointed Prince of Huaiyang Yu grand commander of all armies for the northern campaign to attack Poluhan Baleng.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, Wei made Prince of Huaiyang Yuan Yu commander-in-chief of the northern expedition to attack Poluhan Baleng.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，高平鎮民赫連恩等反，推敕勒酋長胡琛為高平王，攻高平鎮以應拔陵。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, the people of Gaoping Garrison—Helian En and others—rebelled, set up the Tiele chieftain Hu Chen as King of Gaoping, and attacked Gaoping Garrison to support Baleng.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, the people of Gaoping Garrison rebelled under Helian En and others. They installed the Tiele chieftain Hu Chen as King of Gaoping and attacked Gaoping Garrison in concert with Baleng.

sentences.zh: 魏將盧祖遷擊破之，琛北走。

translations.literal: The Wei general Lu Zuqian defeated them, and Chen fled north.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei general Lu Zuqian routed them, and Hu Chen fled north.

sentences.zh: 衛可孤攻懷朔鎮經年，外援不至，楊鈞使賀拔勝詣臨淮王彧告急。

translations.literal: Wei Kehu had besieged Huaishuo Garrison for a year; outside relief did not arrive. Yang Jun sent Heba Sheng to Prince of Huaiyang Yu to report the emergency.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Kehu had besieged Huaishuo Garrison for a year without outside relief arriving. Yang Jun sent Heba Sheng to Prince of Huaiyang Yuan Yu to plead for help.

sentences.zh: 勝募敢死少年十餘騎，夜伺隙潰圍出，賊騎追及之，勝曰：「我賀拔破胡也。

translations.literal: Sheng recruited more than ten daredevil youths on horseback; by night he watched for an opening and broke out of the encirclement. Rebel horsemen caught up with him, and Sheng said, "I am Heba Pohu.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng raised a dozen-odd daredevil youths on horseback and, by night, seized an opening to break out of the siege. Rebel cavalry overtook him, and Sheng cried, "I am Heba Pohu!

sentences.zh: 」賊不敢逼。

translations.literal: " The rebels did not dare press him.
translations.idiomatic: " The rebels did not dare close in.

sentences.zh: 勝見彧於雲中，說之曰：「懷朔被圍，旦夕淪陷，大王今頓兵不進；

translations.literal: Sheng saw Yu at Yunzhong and urged him, saying, "Huaishuo is besieged and will fall at any moment, yet Your Highness now halts your army and does not advance;
translations.idiomatic: Sheng met Yuan Yu at Yunzhong and urged him: "Huaishuo is under siege and will fall at any moment, yet Your Highness holds your army back and will not advance;

sentences.zh: 懷朔若陷，則武川亦危，賊之銳氣百倍，雖有良、平，不能為大王計矣。

translations.literal: if Huaishuo falls, Wuchuan will also be in peril, and the rebels' fighting spirit will be a hundredfold. Even with a Liang or a Ping, they could not devise a plan for Your Highness.
translations.idiomatic: if Huaishuo falls, Wuchuan will be in peril too, and the rebels' fighting spirit will multiply a hundredfold. Even Liang and Ping together could not plot a way out for Your Highness.

sentences.zh: 」彧許為出師，勝還，復突圍而入。

translations.literal: " Yu promised to march out; Sheng returned and again broke through the encirclement to enter.
translations.idiomatic: " Yuan Yu promised to take the field. Sheng went back and broke through the siege lines once more to re-enter the garrison.

sentences.zh: 鈞復遣勝出覘武川，武川已陷。

translations.literal: Jun again sent Sheng out to reconnoiter Wuchuan; Wuchuan had already fallen.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jun sent Sheng out again to scout Wuchuan, but Wuchuan had already fallen.

sentences.zh: 勝馳還，懷朔亦潰，勝父子俱為可孤所虜。

translations.literal: Sheng galloped back, but Huaishuo had also collapsed, and Sheng and his father and son were both taken captive by Kehu.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng raced back, only to find Huaishuo had collapsed as well. He and his father and son were all taken captive by Wei Kehu.

sentences.zh: 五月，臨淮王彧與破六韓拔陵戰於五原，兵敗，彧坐削除官爵。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, Prince of Huaiyang Yu fought Poluhan Baleng at Wuyuan, was defeated, and on that account was stripped of office and rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, Prince of Huaiyang Yuan Yu fought Poluhan Baleng at Wuyuan, was defeated, and was stripped of office and rank on that account.

sentences.zh: 安北將軍隴西李叔仁又敗於白道，賊勢日盛。

translations.literal: The Anbei General Li Shuren of Longxi was again defeated on the White Road, and the rebels' power grew daily.
translations.idiomatic: Anbei General Li Shuren of Longxi was defeated again on the White Road, and the rebels grew stronger by the day.

sentences.zh: 魏主引丞相、令、僕、尚書、侍中、黃門於顯陽殿，問之曰：「今寇連恆、朔，逼近金陵，計將安出？

translations.literal: The Wei ruler summoned the Chancellor, the Ministers, the Masters of Writing, the Attendants-in-Ordinary, and the Yellow Gate Attendants to the Hall of Manifest Yang and asked them, saying, "Now the bandits link Heng and Shuo and draw near the capital precincts—what plan shall we adopt?
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor summoned the chancellor, ministers, masters of writing, attendants-in-ordinary, and yellow-gate attendants to the Hall of Manifest Yang and asked: "The rebels now hold Heng and Shuo in succession and press upon the capital—what is to be done?

sentences.zh: 」吏部尚書元修義請遣重臣督軍鎮恆、朔以捍寇。

translations.literal: " The Minister of the Ministry of Personnel Yuan Xiuyi asked that a high minister be sent to supervise the army and garrison Heng and Shuo to repel the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: " Minister of Personnel Yuan Xiuyi proposed sending a senior minister to take command and hold Heng and Shuo against the rebels.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「去歲阿那瑰叛亂，遣李崇北征，崇上表求改鎮為州，朕以舊章難革，不從其請。

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Last year Anagui rebelled; I sent Li Chong on a northern expedition. Chong memorialized asking to change the garrisons into prefectures. I held that the old statutes were hard to alter and did not follow his request.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Last year, when Anagui rebelled, I sent Li Chong on a northern campaign. Chong memorialized asking that the garrisons be turned into prefectures. I held that the old statutes were hard to change and did not grant his request.

sentences.zh: 尋崇此表，開鎮戶非翼之心，致有今日之患；

translations.literal: Soon afterward Chong's memorial opened the garrison households' hearts to discontent, bringing about today's calamity;
translations.idiomatic: In retrospect, that memorial of Chong's stirred the garrison households' hearts toward discontent and brought on today's disaster;

sentences.zh: 但既往難追，聊復略論耳。

translations.literal: but what is past cannot be pursued—let us speak of it only in brief.
translations.idiomatic: but what is past cannot be undone—let us touch on it only briefly.

sentences.zh: 然崇貴戚重望，器識英敏，意欲還遣崇行，何如？

translations.literal: Yet Chong is a noble kinsman of weighty reputation, talented and keen of mind. I intend to send Chong out again—what do you think?
translations.idiomatic: Yet Chong is a kinsman of high standing, talented and keen of mind. I mean to send Chong north again—what do you think?

sentences.zh: 」僕射蕭寶寅等皆曰：「如此，實合群望。

translations.literal: " The Pushe Xiao Baoyin and the others all said, "If it is so, it truly accords with the hopes of all.
translations.idiomatic: " Pushe Xiao Baoyin and the others all said, "If it is done so, it will truly satisfy everyone's hopes.

sentences.zh: 」崇曰：「臣以六鎮遐僻，密邇寇戎，欲以慰悅彼心，豈敢導之為亂！

translations.literal: " Chong said, "Your servant, because the Six Garrisons are remote and border on the barbarian foe, wished to soothe and please their hearts—how would I dare to lead them into rebellion!
translations.idiomatic: " Li Chong said, "Your servant, seeing how remote the Six Garrisons are and how close they lie to the barbarian frontier, wished only to soothe their hearts—how would I dare to incite them to rebellion!

sentences.zh: 臣罪當就死，陛下赦之；

translations.literal: Your servant's crime deserved death, yet Your Majesty pardoned me;
translations.idiomatic: Your servant deserved death for his crime, yet Your Majesty spared him;

sentences.zh: 今更遣臣北行，正是報恩改過之秋。

translations.literal: to send your servant north again now is precisely the season to repay grace and amend faults.
translations.idiomatic: to send your servant north again now is precisely the time to repay grace and make amends.

sentences.zh: 但臣年七十，加之疲病，不堪軍旅，願更擇賢材。

translations.literal: But your servant is seventy years old, and with weariness and illness added, I cannot bear the rigors of campaign. I wish that another worthy be chosen.
translations.idiomatic: But your servant is seventy years old, and with weariness and illness on top of that, I cannot bear the rigors of campaign. I beg that another worthy be chosen.

sentences.zh: 」帝不許。

translations.literal: " The emperor did not consent.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor would not agree.

sentences.zh: 修義，天賜之子也。

translations.literal: Xiuyi was the son of Tiansi.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuyi was the son of Tiansi.

sentences.zh: 臣光曰：李崇之表，乃所以銷禍於未萌，制勝於無形。

translations.literal: Your subject Guang says: Li Chong's memorial was precisely the means to quell disaster before it sprouted and to prevail in the formless.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject Guang remarks: Li Chong's memorial was precisely the means to quell disaster before it sprouted and to prevail before shape could be seen.

sentences.zh: 魏肅宗既不能用，及亂生之日，曾無愧謝之言，乃更以為崇罪。

translations.literal: Emperor Suzong of Wei, having been unable to employ it, when the day of rebellion came had not a word of shame or apology, but instead made Chong's crime the greater.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Suzong of Wei could not adopt it; when rebellion broke out he offered not a word of shame or apology, but instead laid the blame on Chong.

sentences.zh: 彼不明之君，烏可與謀哉！

translations.literal: Such an unenlightened ruler—how could one plot with him!
translations.idiomatic: With such an unenlightened ruler, how could one take counsel together!

sentences.zh: 《詩》云：「聽言則對，誦言如醉，匪用其良，覆俾我悖。

translations.literal: The Odes say, "When he hears words he answers; when words are recited he is as if drunk. He does not employ the good, but overturns and makes us perverse."
translations.idiomatic: The Odes say: "He answers when he hears words; he is as if drunk when words are recited. He does not use the good, but overturns and makes us perverse."

sentences.zh: 」其是之謂矣。

translations.literal: " This is what is meant.
translations.idiomatic: " This is what is meant.

sentences.zh: 壬申，加崇使持節、開府儀同三司、北討大都督，命撫軍將軍崔暹、鎮軍將軍廣陽王深皆受崇節度。

translations.literal: On the day renshen, Chong was advanced to Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon of the First Order, and Grand Commander of the Northern Campaign. The Fugun General Cui Xian and the Zhenjun General Prince of Guangyang Shen were both ordered to accept Chong's command.
translations.idiomatic: On the day renshen, Li Chong was promoted to bearer of the staff of authority, grand master with golden seal and purple ribbon of the first order, and grand commander of the northern campaign. Fugun General Cui Xian and Zhenjun General Prince of Guangyang Yuan Shen were both placed under Chong's command.

sentences.zh: 深，嘉之子也。

translations.literal: Shen was the son of Jia.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shen was the son of Jia.

sentences.zh: 六月，以豫州刺史裴邃督征討諸軍事，以伐魏。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, Inspector of Yuzhou Pei Sui was made commander of all armies for punitive expedition to attack Wei.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, Inspector of Yuzhou Pei Sui was appointed commander of the punitive expedition against Wei.

sentences.zh: 魏自破六韓拔陵之反，二夏、豳、涼寇盜蜂起。

translations.literal: From the time of Poluhan Baleng's rebellion in Wei, bandits and robbers rose like hornets in the two Xia regions, Bin, and Liang.
translations.idiomatic: After Poluhan Baleng's rebellion in Wei, bandits and raiders swarmed up in the two Xia regions, Bin, and Liang.

sentences.zh: 秦州刺史李彥，政刑殘虐，在下皆怨。

translations.literal: Li Yan, Inspector of Qinzhou, was cruel in government and punishment; those below all resented him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yan, inspector of Qinzhou, was brutal in government and punishment, and all beneath him resented him.

sentences.zh: 是月，城內薛珍等聚黨突入州門，擒彥，殺之，推其黨莫折大提為帥，大提自稱秦王。

translations.literal: That month, Xue Zhen and others within the city gathered a faction, burst into the prefectural gate, seized Yan, and killed him. They set up their comrade Mozhe Dati as leader; Dati styled himself King of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: That month, Xue Zhen and others in the city rallied a faction, stormed the prefectural gate, seized Yan, and killed him. They installed their comrade Mozhe Dati as leader, and Dati styled himself King of Qin.

sentences.zh: 魏遣雍州刺史元志討之。

translations.literal: Wei sent Yuan Zhi, Inspector of Yongzhou, to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: Wei sent Yuan Zhi, inspector of Yongzhou, to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 初，南秦州豪右楊松柏兄弟，數為寇盜，刺史博陵崔游誘之使降，引為主簿，接以辭色，使說下群氐，既而因宴會盡收斬之，由是所部莫不猜懼。

translations.literal: Earlier, the powerful families of Southern Qinzhou—the brothers Yang Songbai—had repeatedly been bandits and robbers. The Inspector Cui You of Boling enticed them to surrender, brought them in as chief clerks, treated them with courteous words and countenance, and had them persuade the Di clans below to submit. Then, taking advantage of a banquet, he seized and beheaded them all. From this, none in his jurisdiction was without suspicion and fear.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the powerful Yang Songbai brothers of Southern Qinzhou had repeatedly turned bandit. Inspector Cui You of Boling lured them into surrender, took them on as chief clerks, treated them with courtesy, and set them to win over the Di clans. Then, at a banquet, he seized and beheaded them all. From that day, everyone under his rule lived in suspicion and fear.

sentences.zh: 游聞李彥死，自知不安，欲逃去，未果；

translations.literal: When You heard that Li Yan was dead, he knew himself unsafe and wished to flee, but did not succeed;
translations.idiomatic: When Cui You heard that Li Yan was dead, he knew he was unsafe and tried to flee, but could not;

sentences.zh: 城民張長命、韓祖香、孫掩等攻游，殺之，以城應大提。

translations.literal: the townspeople Zhang Changming, Han Zuxiang, Sun Yan, and others attacked You and killed him, then offered the city to Dati.
translations.idiomatic: the townspeople Zhang Changming, Han Zuxiang, Sun Yan, and others attacked You, killed him, and surrendered the city to Dati.

sentences.zh: 大提遺其黨卜胡襲高平，克之，殺鎮將赫連略、行台高元榮。

translations.literal: Dati sent his follower Bu Hu to strike Gaoping, took it, and killed the garrison commander Helian Lüe and the itinerant commissioner Gao Yuanrong.
translations.idiomatic: Dati sent his follower Bu Hu against Gaoping, took it, and killed Garrison Commander Helian Lüe and itinerant commissioner Gao Yuanrong.

sentences.zh: 大提尋卒，子念生自稱天子，置百官，改元天建。

translations.literal: Dati soon died. His son Niansheng styled himself Son of Heaven, established the hundred offices, and changed the era name to Tianjian.
translations.idiomatic: Dati soon died. His son Niansheng styled himself Son of Heaven, set up the full bureaucracy, and changed the era name to Tianjian.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，魏大赦。

translations.literal: On the day dingyou, Wei proclaimed a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: On the day dingyou, Wei proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，甲寅，魏遣吏部尚書元修義兼尚書僕射，為西道行台，帥諸將討莫折念生。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on the day jiayin, Wei sent Yuan Xiuyi, Minister of the Ministry of Personnel, also serving as Master of Writing and Deputy Director, as itinerant commissioner of the Western Route to lead the generals against Mozhe Niansheng.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on the day jiayin, Wei sent Yuan Xiuyi, minister of personnel, also serving as master of writing and deputy director, as itinerant commissioner of the western route to lead the generals against Mozhe Niansheng.

sentences.zh: 崔暹違李崇節度，與破六韓拔陵戰於白道，大敗，單騎走還。

translations.literal: Cui Xian disobeyed Li Chong's command, fought Poluhan Baleng on the White Road, was utterly defeated, and fled back alone on horseback.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Xian disobeyed Li Chong's orders, fought Poluhan Baleng on the White Road, was routed, and fled back alone on horseback.

sentences.zh: 拔陵並力攻崇，崇力戰不能御，引還雲中，與之相持。

translations.literal: Baleng combined his forces to attack Chong. Chong fought hard but could not withstand him, drew back to Yunzhong, and faced him in stalemate.
translations.idiomatic: Baleng combined his forces to attack Chong. Chong fought hard but could not hold him off, withdrew to Yunzhong, and faced him in stalemate.

sentences.zh: 廣相王深上言：「先朝都平城，以北邊為重，盛簡親賢，擁麾作鎮，配以高門子弟，以死防遏，非唯不廢仕宦，乃更獨得復除，當時人物，忻慕為之。

translations.literal: Prince of Guangyang Shen memorialized, saying, "The former court made its capital at Pingcheng and regarded the northern frontier as weighty. It lavishly selected kinsmen and worthies, gave them banners and made them garrison commanders, paired them with sons of eminent houses, and had them die to hold the line. Not only were they not deprived of office; they alone also received exemption from corvée. Men of the time rejoiced and admired this.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Guangyang Yuan Shen memorialized: "The former court made its capital at Pingcheng and treated the northern frontier as paramount. It lavishly chose kinsmen and worthies, gave them banners and made them garrison commanders, paired them with sons of eminent houses, and had them die holding the line. Not only were they not barred from office; they alone also received exemption from corvée. Men of the time looked on it with admiration.

sentences.zh: 太和中，僕射李沖用事，涼州土人悉免廝役；

translations.literal: In the Taihe era, the Pushe Li Chong held power, and the native people of Liangzhou were all exempted from menial service;
translations.idiomatic: In the Taihe era, Pushe Li Chong held power, and the native people of Liangzhou were all exempted from menial service;

sentences.zh: 帝鄉舊門，仍防邊戍，自非得罪當世，莫肯與之為伍。

translations.literal: the old houses of the imperial domain still guarded the frontier garrisons. Unless one had offended the age, none would join them as companions.
translations.idiomatic: the old houses of the imperial domain still manned the frontier garrisons. Unless one had fallen foul of the age, none would join them as equals.

sentences.zh: 本鎮驅使，但為虞候、白直，一生推遷，不過軍主；

translations.literal: Those driven in service at the home garrison were only scouts and day-duty men; in a lifetime of promotion they did not rise above garrison commander;
translations.idiomatic: those driven in service at the home garrison were only scouts and day-duty men; in a lifetime of promotion they rose no higher than garrison commander;

sentences.zh: 然其同族留京師者得上品通官，在鎮者即為清途所隔，或多逃逸。

translations.literal: yet their kinsmen who remained in the capital could obtain high-grade regular offices, while those at the garrisons were cut off from the clear path and many fled.
translations.idiomatic: yet their kinsmen who stayed in the capital could obtain high-grade regular offices, while those at the garrisons were shut out of the clear path to advancement, and many fled.

sentences.zh: 乃峻邊兵之格，鎮人不聽浮游在外，於是少年不得從師，長者不得游宦，獨為匪人，言之流涕！

translations.literal: Then the standards for frontier soldiers were made severe; garrison people were not permitted to wander outside, so youths could not follow teachers and elders could not seek office elsewhere—they were left only as outlaws. To speak of it brings tears to the eyes!
translations.idiomatic: Then the standards for frontier soldiers were tightened; garrison people were forbidden to wander abroad, so youths could not study under teachers and elders could not seek office elsewhere—they were left only as outlaws. To speak of it brings tears to the eyes!

sentences.zh: 自定鼎伊、洛，邊任益輕，唯底滯凡才，乃出為鎮將，轉相模習，專事聚斂。

translations.literal: From the time the tripod was fixed at Yi and Luo, frontier appointments grew ever lighter; only the stagnant and mediocre were sent out as garrison generals, imitating one another in turn and devoting themselves solely to amassing wealth.
translations.idiomatic: From the time the capital was fixed at Luoyang, frontier appointments grew ever lighter; only the stagnant and mediocre were sent out as garrison generals, imitating one another and devoting themselves solely to amassing wealth.

sentences.zh: 或諸方奸吏，犯罪配邊，為之指蹤，政以賄立，邊人無不切齒。

translations.literal: Or corrupt officials from various regions, convicted and assigned to the frontier, directed their tracks for them; government was established by bribes, and the frontier people none but gnashed their teeth.
translations.idiomatic: Or corrupt officials from various regions, convicted and assigned to the frontier, showed them the way; government was bought with bribes, and the frontier people gnashed their teeth at it.

sentences.zh: 及阿那瑰背恩縱掠，發奔命追之，十五萬眾度沙漠，不日而還。

translations.literal: When Anagui turned ungrateful and let his men plunder, an army of a hundred and fifty thousand crossed the desert on urgent summons to pursue him and returned within days.
translations.idiomatic: When Anagui turned ungrateful and let his men plunder, an army of a hundred and fifty thousand crossed the desert on urgent summons to pursue him and returned within days.

sentences.zh: 邊人見此援師，遂自意輕中國。

translations.literal: The frontier people, seeing these relief troops, then took it upon themselves to look lightly on the Middle Kingdom.
translations.idiomatic: The frontier people, seeing these relief troops, then took it upon themselves to look lightly on the empire.

sentences.zh: 尚書令臣崇求改鎮為州，抑亦先覺，朝廷未許。

translations.literal: Your servant Chong, Minister of the Masters of Writing, asked to change the garrisons into prefectures—this too was foresight—but the court did not grant it.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant Chong, minister of the masters of writing, asked to change the garrisons into prefectures—this too was foresight—but the court did not grant it.

sentences.zh: 而高闕戍主御下失和，拔陵殺之，遂相帥為亂，攻城掠地，所過夷滅，王師屢北，賊黨日盛。

translations.literal: Then the garrison chief of Gaogue lost harmony in ruling those below; Baleng killed him, and they led one another into rebellion, storming cities and seizing land, leveling all they passed. The royal army was repeatedly beaten north, and the rebel faction grew daily.
translations.idiomatic: Then the garrison chief of Gaogue lost harmony in ruling those below; Baleng killed him, and they led one another into rebellion, storming cities and seizing land and leveling all they passed. The royal army was repeatedly beaten back, and the rebel faction grew daily.

sentences.zh: 此段之舉，指望銷平；

translations.literal: This present campaign was looked to for quelling and pacification;
translations.idiomatic: This present campaign was expected to quell the trouble;

sentences.zh: 而崔暹只輪不返，臣崇與臣逡巡復路，相與還次雲中，將士之情莫不解體。

translations.literal: yet Cui Xian did not return even with a single wheel, and your servant Chong and your servant hesitated on the road back, returning together to encamp at Yunzhong. The feelings of officers and soldiers were all without exception undone.
translations.idiomatic: yet Cui Xian did not return even with a single wheel intact, and your servant Chong and your servant hesitated on the road back, returning together to encamp at Yunzhong. The morale of officers and soldiers was utterly shattered.

sentences.zh: 今日所慮，非止西北，將恐諸鎮尋亦如此，天下之事，何易可量！

translations.literal: What is feared today is not only the northwest; I fear the other garrisons will soon be the same. The affairs of the realm—how easily can they be measured!
translations.idiomatic: What is feared today is not only the northwest; I fear the other garrisons will soon follow suit. The affairs of the realm—how easily can they be measured!

sentences.zh: 」書奏，不省。

translations.literal: " The memorial was submitted; it was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: " The memorial was submitted; it went unheeded.

sentences.zh: 詔征崔暹系廷尉；

translations.literal: An edict ordered Cui Xian summoned and bound over to the Court of the Imperial Clan;
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Cui Xian summoned and bound over to the Court of the Imperial Clan;

sentences.zh: 暹以女妓、田園賂元義，卒得不坐。

translations.literal: Xian bribed Yuan Yi with female entertainers and estates and in the end was not punished.
translations.idiomatic: Xian bribed Yuan Yi with female entertainers and estates and in the end escaped punishment.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，莫折念生遣其都督楊伯年等攻仇鳩、河池二戍，東益州刺史魏子建遣將軍伊祥等擊破之，斬首千餘級。

translations.literal: On the day dingchou, Mozhe Niansheng sent his commander Yang Bonian and others to attack the two garrisons of Qiuchiu and Hechi. Wei Zijian, Inspector of Eastern Yizhou, sent the generals Yi Xiang and others to defeat them and took more than a thousand heads.
translations.idiomatic: On the day dingchou, Mozhe Niansheng sent his commander Yang Bonian and others to attack the garrisons of Qiuchiu and Hechi. Wei Zijian, inspector of eastern Yizhou, sent Generals Yi Xiang and others to rout them and took more than a thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 東益州本氐王楊紹先之國，將佐皆以城民勁勇，二秦反者皆其族類，請先收其器械。

translations.literal: Eastern Yizhou was originally the domain of the Di king Yang Shaoxian. The officers all said the townspeople were fierce and brave, and the rebels of the two Qin regions were all their clansmen; they asked first to seize their weapons.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Yizhou had originally been the domain of the Di king Yang Shaoxian. The officers all said the townspeople were fierce and brave and that the rebels of the two Qin regions were their clansmen; they asked first to seize their weapons.

sentences.zh: 子建曰：「城民數經行陣，撫之足以為用，急之則腹背為患。

translations.literal: Zijian said, "The townspeople have repeatedly seen battle lines; if soothed they are sufficient for use. If pressed, they will be a trouble at front and back.
translations.idiomatic: Zijian said, "The townspeople have repeatedly seen battle; if treated well they are fit for use. If pressed hard, they will become a danger front and rear.

sentences.zh: 」乃悉召城民，慰諭之，既而漸分其父兄子弟外戍諸郡，內外相顧，卒無叛者。

translations.literal: " He then summoned all the townspeople, comforted and instructed them, and afterward gradually divided their fathers, elder brothers, sons, and younger brothers to garrison the various commanderies outside. With inside and outside watching one another, in the end there were none who rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: " He then summoned all the townspeople, comforted and instructed them, and afterward gradually posted their fathers, elder brothers, sons, and younger brothers to garrison various commanderies outside. With inside and outside keeping watch on one another, in the end none rebelled.

sentences.zh: 子建，蘭根之族兄也。

translations.literal: Zijian was a clansman elder brother of Langan.
translations.idiomatic: Zijian was a cousin of Langan.

sentences.zh: 魏涼州幢帥於菩提等執刺史宋穎，據州反。

translations.literal: In Wei, the Liangzhou standard-bearer Yiputi and others seized Inspector Song Ying, held the province, and rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: In Wei, the Liangzhou standard-bearer Yiputi and others seized Inspector Song Ying, seized the province, and rebelled.

sentences.zh: 八月，庚寅，徐州刺史成景俊拔魏童城。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on the day gengyin, Cheng Jingjun, Inspector of Xuzhou, took Wei's Tongcheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on the day gengyin, Cheng Jingjun, inspector of Xuzhou, took Wei's Tongcheng.

sentences.zh: 魏員外散騎侍郎李苗上書曰：「凡食少兵精，利於速戰；

translations.literal: Li Miao, Supernumerary Attendant Cavalier of the Wei, memorialized, saying, "In general, little food and elite troops favor swift battle;
translations.idiomatic: Li Miao, supernumerary attendant cavalier of Wei, memorialized: "In general, little food and elite troops favor swift battle;

sentences.zh: 糧多卒眾，事宜持久。

translations.literal: much grain and many soldiers suit prolonged warfare.
translations.idiomatic: much grain and many soldiers suit prolonged warfare.

sentences.zh: 今隴賊猖狂，非有素蓄，雖據兩城，本無德義。

translations.literal: Now the Long bandits are rampant, but they have no long-standing stores; though they hold two cities, they fundamentally lack virtue and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Now the Long rebels are rampant, but they have no long-standing stores; though they hold two cities, they fundamentally lack virtue and righteousness.

sentences.zh: 其勢在於疾攻，日有降納，遲則人情離沮，坐待崩潰。

translations.literal: Their momentum lies in swift attack; day by day there are surrenders and submissions. If delayed, men's hearts will separate and flag, and one may sit and await their collapse.
translations.idiomatic: Their momentum lies in swift attack; day by day there are surrenders. If delayed, morale will fray, and one may sit and await their collapse.

sentences.zh: 夫飆至風舉，逆者求萬一之功；

translations.literal: When the whirlwind comes and the gale rises, those who oppose it seek a one-in-ten-thousand success;
translations.idiomatic: When the whirlwind comes and the gale rises, those who oppose it seek a one-in-ten-thousand success;

sentences.zh: 高壁深壘，王師有全制之策。

translations.literal: with high walls and deep ramparts, the royal army has the policy of complete control.
translations.idiomatic: with high walls and deep ramparts, the royal army has the policy of complete control.

sentences.zh: 但天下久泰，人不曉兵，奔利不相待，逃難不相顧，將無法令，士非教習，不思長久之計，各有輕敵之心。

translations.literal: But the realm has long been at peace; people do not understand warfare. In rushing for profit they do not wait for one another; in fleeing danger they do not look back for one another. Generals lack laws and orders; soldiers lack training and drill. They do not think of long-term plans and each has a heart that lightly esteems the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: But the realm has long been at peace and people do not understand warfare. In rushing for profit they do not wait for one another; in fleeing danger they do not look back for one another. Generals lack discipline; soldiers lack training. They do not think of long-term plans, and each harbors contempt for the enemy.

sentences.zh: 如令隴東不守，汧軍敗散，則兩秦遂強，三輔危弱，國之右臂於斯廢矣。

translations.literal: If Longdong is not held and the Qian army is defeated and scattered, then the two Qin regions will grow strong, the Three Assistants will be perilous and weak, and the state's right arm will be abandoned at this point.
translations.idiomatic: If Longdong is not held and the Qian army is defeated and scattered, the two Qin regions will grow strong, the Three Assistants will be perilous and weak, and the state's right arm will be lost at a stroke.

sentences.zh: 宜勒大將堅壁勿戰，別命偏裨帥精兵數千出麥積崖以襲其後，則汧、岐之下，群妖自散。

translations.literal: The great general should be ordered to hold the walls firm and not fight; separately command a deputy to lead several thousand elite troops out from Maiji Cliff to strike their rear—then below Qian and Qi the demon hosts will scatter of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: The great general should be ordered to hold the walls firm and not fight; a deputy should be sent with several thousand elite troops out from Maiji Cliff to strike their rear—then below Qian and Qi the rebel hosts will scatter of themselves.

sentences.zh: 魏以苗為統軍，與別將淳於誕俱出梁、益，隸魏子建。

translations.literal: Wei made Miao a commander-in-chief; together with the separate general Chunyu Dan he marched out from Liang and Yi and was placed under Wei Zijian.
translations.idiomatic: Wei made Li Miao a commander-in-chief; together with the separate general Chunyu Dan he marched out from Liang and Yi and was placed under Wei Zijian.

sentences.zh: 未至，莫折念生遣其弟高陽王天生將兵下隴。

translations.literal: Before they arrived, Mozhe Niansheng sent his younger brother, Prince of Gaoyang Tiansheng, to lead troops down from Long.
translations.idiomatic: Before they arrived, Mozhe Niansheng sent his younger brother, Prince of Gaoyang Tiansheng, to lead troops down from Long.

sentences.zh: 甲午，都督元志與戰於隴口，志兵敗，棄眾東保岐州。

translations.literal: On the day jiawu, the Commander Yuan Zhi fought him at Longkou. Zhi's army was defeated; he abandoned the host and went east to hold Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: On the day jiawu, Commander Yuan Zhi fought him at Longkou. Zhi's army was defeated; he abandoned his troops and withdrew east to hold Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 東西部敕勒皆叛魏，附於破六韓拔陵，魏主始思李崇及廣陽王深之言。

translations.literal: The eastern and western Tiele all rebelled against Wei and attached themselves to Poluhan Baleng. The Wei ruler at last recalled the words of Li Chong and Prince of Guangyang Shen.
translations.idiomatic: The eastern and western Tiele all rebelled against Wei and joined Poluhan Baleng. The Wei emperor at last recalled the words of Li Chong and Prince of Guangyang Yuan Shen.

sentences.zh: 丙申，下詔：「諸州鎮軍貫非有罪配隸者，皆免為民。

translations.literal: On the day bingshen, an edict was issued: "All garrison soldiers of the various prefectures who were not originally convicts assigned to service are all freed to be commoners.
translations.idiomatic: On the day bingshen, an edict was issued: "All garrison soldiers of the various prefectures who were not originally convicts assigned to service are all freed to be commoners.

sentences.zh: 」改鎮為州，以懷朔鎮為朔州，更命朔州白雲州。

translations.literal: " The garrisons were changed into prefectures; Huaishuo Garrison was made Shuzhou, and Shuzhou was renamed Baiyunzhou.
translations.idiomatic: " The garrisons were changed into prefectures; Huaishuo Garrison was made Shuzhou, and Shuzhou was renamed Baiyunzhou.

sentences.zh: 遣兼黃門侍郎酈道元為大使，撫慰六鎮。

translations.literal: The Concurrent Yellow Gate Attendant Li Daoyuan was sent as grand envoy to soothe the Six Garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: Concurrent yellow-gate attendant Li Daoyuan was sent as grand envoy to soothe the Six Garrisons.

sentences.zh: 時六鎮已盡叛，道元不果行。

translations.literal: At that time the Six Garrisons had all rebelled; Daoyuan did not succeed in going.
translations.idiomatic: By then the Six Garrisons had all rebelled, and Li Daoyuan never made the journey.

sentences.zh: 先是，代人遷洛者，多為選部所抑，不得仕進。

translations.literal: Earlier, those of the Dai people who had moved to Luoyang were mostly suppressed by the Selection Bureau and could not advance in office.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, those of the Dai people who had moved to Luoyang were mostly blocked by the Selection Bureau and could not advance in office.

sentences.zh: 及六鎮叛，元義乃用代來寒人為傳詔以尉悅之。

translations.literal: When the Six Garrisons rebelled, Yuan Yi then employed poor men of Dai origin who had come to serve as edict-bearers to soothe and please them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Six Garrisons rebelled, Yuan Yi then employed poor men of Dai origin who had come to Luoyang as edict-bearers to soothe and please them.

sentences.zh: 廷尉評代人山偉奏記，稱義德美，義摧偉為尚書二千石郎。

translations.literal: Shan Wei of the Dai people, an evaluator in the Court of the Imperial Clan, submitted a note praising Yi's virtue and beauty; Yi promoted Wei to Lang of the Masters of Writing at the two-thousand-bushel grade.
translations.idiomatic: Shan Wei of the Dai people, an evaluator in the Court of the Imperial Clan, submitted a note praising Yi's virtue; Yi promoted Wei to a lang of the masters of writing at the two-thousand-bushel grade.

sentences.zh: 秀容人乞伏莫於聚眾攻郡，殺太守；

translations.literal: Qifu Moyu of Xiurong gathered a crowd, attacked the commandery, and killed the grand administrator;
translations.idiomatic: Qifu Moyu of Xiurong gathered a crowd, attacked the commandery, and killed the grand administrator;

sentences.zh: 丁酉，南秀容牧子萬於乞真反，殺太僕卿陸延，秀容酋長爾朱榮討平之。

translations.literal: On dingyou, Wan Yuqizhen, a herdsman of South Xiurong, rebelled, killed Grand Steward Lu Yan, and Xiurong chieftain Erzhu Rong suppressed and pacified him.
translations.idiomatic: On the dingyou day, Wan Yuqizhen, a herdsman of South Xiurong, rose in rebellion and slew Grand Steward Lu Yan; Erzhu Rong, chieftain of Xiurong, marched against him and put the revolt down.

sentences.zh: 榮，羽健之玄孫也。

translations.literal: Rong was the great-grandson of Yu Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Rong was a great-grandson of Yu Jian.

sentences.zh: 其祖代勤，嘗出獵，部民射虎，誤中其髀，代勤拔箭，不復推問，所部莫不感悅。

translations.literal: His grandfather Dai Qin once went hunting; his tribesmen, shooting at a tiger, mistakenly struck his thigh; Dai Qin drew out the arrow and pursued the matter no further, and all who served under him were moved and pleased.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Dai Qin had once gone hunting when his tribesmen, firing at a tiger, accidentally struck him in the thigh. Dai Qin drew out the arrow and asked no further questions; all who served under him were deeply moved.

sentences.zh: 官至肆州刺史，賜爵染郡公，年九十餘而卒；

translations.literal: He reached the office of Governor of Sizhou, was granted the title Duke of Randu, and died at more than ninety years of age;
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Governor of Sizhou and was enfeoffed as Duke of Randu; he died at more than ninety years of age.

sentences.zh: 子新興立。

translations.literal: His son Xinxing succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xinxing succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 新興時，畜牧尤蕃息，牛羊駝馬，色別為群，瀰漫川谷，不可勝數。

translations.literal: In Xinxing's time livestock flourished especially; cattle, sheep, camels, and horses, sorted by color into herds, filled the valleys and hills beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Under Xinxing the herds multiplied abundantly—cattle, sheep, camels, and horses grouped by color, covering valleys and hills in numbers beyond reckoning.

sentences.zh: 魏每出師，新興輒獻馬及資糧以助軍，高祖嘉之。

translations.literal: Whenever Wei took the field, Xinxing always presented horses and provisions to aid the army, and Emperor Gaozu commended this.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Wei took the field, Xinxing sent horses and supplies to aid the army, and Emperor Gaozu commended him.

sentences.zh: 新興老，請傳爵於子榮，魏朝許之。

translations.literal: Xinxing grew old and requested to transfer his title to his son Rong; the Wei court granted it.
translations.idiomatic: When Xinxing grew old, he asked to pass his title to his son Rong, and the Wei court assented.

sentences.zh: 榮神機明決，御眾嚴整。

translations.literal: Rong was divine in stratagem and clear in decision; he commanded the multitude with stern order.
translations.idiomatic: Rong was swift of mind and firm in judgment, commanding his followers with stern discipline.

sentences.zh: 時四方兵起，榮陰有大志，散其畜牧資財，招合驍勇，結納豪傑，於是侯景、司馬子如、賈顯度及五原段榮、太安竇泰皆往依之。

translations.literal: At the time armies rose on all sides; Rong secretly harbored great ambitions, distributed his herds and wealth, gathered the fierce and brave, and allied with heroes—whereupon Hou Jing, Sima Ziru, Jia Xiandu, Duan Rong of Wuyuan, and Dou Tai of Tai'an all went to rely on him.
translations.idiomatic: As war erupted across the land, Rong nursed secret ambitions. He dispersed his herds and wealth, rallied the bold, and won over champions—whereupon Hou Jing, Sima Ziru, Jia Xiandu, Duan Rong of Wuyuan, and Dou Tai of Tai'an all came to join him.

sentences.zh: 顯度，顯智之兄也。

translations.literal: Xiandu was the elder brother of Xianzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Xiandu was the elder brother of Xianzhi.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，莫折念生遣都督竇雙攻魏盤頭郡，東益州刺史魏子建遣將軍竇念祖擊破之。

translations.literal: On wuxu, Moqi Niansheng sent Commander Dou Shuang to attack Wei's Pantou Commandery; Eastern Yizhou Governor Wei Zijian sent General Dou Nianzu to defeat him.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu, Moqi Niansheng dispatched Commander Dou Shuang against Pantou Commandery; Wei Zijian, Governor of Eastern Yizhou, sent General Dou Nianzu and routed the invaders.

sentences.zh: 九月，戊申，成景俊拔魏睢陵。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on wushen, Cheng Jingjun captured Wei's Suiling.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on wushen, Cheng Jingjun took Suiling from Wei.

sentences.zh: 戊午，北兗州刺史趙景悅圍荊山。

translations.literal: On wuwu, Northern Yanzhou Governor Zhao Jingyue besieged Jingshan.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu, Zhao Jingyue, Governor of Northern Yanzhou, besieged Jingshan.

sentences.zh: 裴邃帥騎三千襲壽陽，壬戌夜，斬關而入，克其外郭。

translations.literal: Pei Sui led three thousand cavalry in a raid on Shouyang; on the night of renxu he cut through the pass and entered, capturing the outer city.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Sui led three thousand horsemen in a surprise attack on Shouyang. On the night of renxu he broke through the gate and seized the outer wall.

sentences.zh: 魏揚州刺史長孫稚御之，一日九戰，後軍蔡秀成失道不至，邃引兵還。

translations.literal: Wei Yangzhou Governor Changsun Zhi resisted him; in one day nine battles were fought; the rear army under Cai Xiucheng lost its way and did not arrive; Sui withdrew his troops.
translations.idiomatic: Changsun Zhi, Wei's Governor of Yangzhou, met him in battle—nine engagements in a single day. When Cai Xiucheng's rear column lost its way and failed to arrive, Sui withdrew.

sentences.zh: 別將擊魏淮陽，魏使行台酈道元、都督河間王琛救壽陽，安樂王鑒救淮陽。

translations.literal: A separate general attacked Wei's Huaiyang; Wei sent Mobile Corps Li Daoyuan and Commander Hejian Prince Chen to rescue Shouyang, and Prince of Anle Jian to rescue Huaiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Another column struck Huaiyang. Wei dispatched Li Daoyuan of the Mobile Corps and Commander Prince Chen of Hejian to relieve Shouyang, and Prince of Anle Jian to relieve Huaiyang.

sentences.zh: 鑒，詮之子也。

translations.literal: Jian was the son of Quan.
translations.idiomatic: Jian was a son of Quan.

sentences.zh: 魏西道行台元修義得風疾，不能治軍。

translations.literal: Wei Western Route Mobile Corps Yuan Xiuyi contracted wind affliction and could not manage the army.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Xiuyi, head of Wei's Western Route Mobile Corps, fell ill with paralysis and could no longer command the army.

sentences.zh: 壬申，魏以尚書左僕射齊王蕭寶寅為西道行台大都督，帥諸將討莫折念生。

translations.literal: On renshen, Wei appointed Left Vice Director of the Secretariat Prince of Qi Xiao Baoyin as Grand Commander of the Western Route Mobile Corps, leading the generals to campaign against Moqi Niansheng.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen, Wei made Left Vice Director of the Secretariat Xiao Baoyin, Prince of Qi, Grand Commander of the Western Route Mobile Corps and sent him with his generals against Moqi Niansheng.

sentences.zh: 宋穎密求救於吐谷渾王伏連籌，伏連籌自將救涼州，於菩提棄城走，追斬之。

translations.literal: Song Ying secretly sought rescue from Tuyuhun King Fu Lianchou; Fu Lianchou personally led troops to save Liangzhou; at Puti he abandoned the city and fled; he was pursued and beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Song Ying secretly appealed to Fu Lianchou, King of Tuyuhun, who marched in person to relieve Liangzhou. At Puti he abandoned the city and fled; pursuers overtook and killed him.

sentences.zh: 城民越天安等復推宋穎為刺史。

translations.literal: City residents Yue Tian'an and others again elevated Song Ying as Governor.
translations.idiomatic: The townspeople, led by Yue Tian'an, once again installed Song Ying as governor.

sentences.zh: 河間王琛軍至西硤石，解渦陽圍，復荊山戍。

translations.literal: Hejian Prince Chen's army reached West Xiashi, lifted the siege of Woyang, and restored the garrison at Jingshan.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Chen of Hejian reached West Xiashi, broke the siege of Woyang, and re-established the garrison at Jingshan.

sentences.zh: 青、冀二州刺史王神念與戰，為琛所敗。

translations.literal: Qing and Ji Governor Wang Shennian fought him and was defeated by Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shennian, Governor of Qing and Ji provinces, engaged him in battle and was defeated by Chen.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，戊寅，裴邃、元樹攻魏建陵城，克之。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on wuyin, Pei Sui and Yuan Shu attacked Wei's Jianling and captured it.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on wuyin, Pei Sui and Yuan Shu attacked Jianling and took it.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，拔曲木，掃虜將軍彭寶孫拔琅邪。

translations.literal: On xinsi, Qumu was taken; General Who Sweeps Barbarians Peng Baosun captured Langye.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi, Qumu fell; General Who Sweeps the Barbarians Peng Baosun seized Langye.

sentences.zh: 魏營州城民劉安定、就德興執史李仲遵，據城反。

translations.literal: Wei Yingzhou city residents Liu Anding and Jiudexing seized Secretary Li Zhongzun and held the city in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Yingzhou, Liu Anding and Jiudexing, seized Secretary Li Zhongzun and rose in rebellion, holding the city.

sentences.zh: 城民王惡兒斬安定以降；

translations.literal: City resident Wang E'er beheaded Anding and surrendered;
translations.idiomatic: A townsman named Wang E'er killed Anding and submitted;

sentences.zh: 德興東走，自稱燕王。

translations.literal: Dexing fled east and styled himself King of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Dexing fled eastward and proclaimed himself King of Yan.

sentences.zh: 胡琛遣其將宿勤明達寂豳、夏、北華三州，壬午，魏遺都督北海王顥帥諸將討之。

translations.literal: Hu Chen sent his general Suqin Mingda to devastate the three provinces of Bin, Xia, and Northern Hua; on renwu, Wei dispatched Commander Beihai Prince Hao leading generals to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Chen sent his general Suqin Mingda to ravage Bin, Xia, and Northern Hua. On renwu, Wei dispatched Commander Prince Hao of Beihai with his generals to campaign against him.

sentences.zh: 顥，詳之子也。

translations.literal: Hao was the son of Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: Hao was a son of Xiang.

sentences.zh: 甲申，彭寶孫拔檀丘。

translations.literal: On jiashen, Peng Baosun captured Tanqiu.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen, Peng Baosun took Tanqiu.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，裴邃拔狄城；

translations.literal: On xinmao, Pei Sui captured Dicheng;
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao, Pei Sui took Dicheng;

sentences.zh: 丙申。

translations.literal: On bingshen.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen,

sentences.zh: 又拔甓城，進屯黎漿。

translations.literal: He again captured Bicheng and advanced to encamp at Lijiang.
translations.idiomatic: he also took Bicheng and encamped at Lijiang.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，魏東海太守韋敬欣以司吾城降。

translations.literal: On renyin, Wei Donghai Administrator Wei Jingxin surrendered Siwu city.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin, Wei Jingxin, Administrator of Donghai, surrendered Siwu.

sentences.zh: 定遠將軍曹世宗拔曲陽；

translations.literal: General Who Establishes Distant Regions Cao Shizong captured Quyang;
translations.idiomatic: General Who Establishes the Distant Cao Shizong took Quyang;

sentences.zh: 甲辰，又拔秦墟，魏守將多棄城走。

translations.literal: On jiachen, he again captured Qinxu; many Wei defending generals abandoned their cities and fled.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen, he also seized Qinxu; many Wei garrison commanders abandoned their posts and fled.

sentences.zh: 魏使黃門侍郎盧同持節詣營州慰勞，就德興降而復反。

translations.literal: Wei sent Yellow Gate Attendant Lu Tong with imperial credentials to Yingzhou to comfort and reward; Jiudexing surrendered but then rebelled again.
translations.idiomatic: Wei sent Yellow Gate Attendant Lu Tong with imperial commission to Yingzhou to offer comfort and rewards; Jiudexing submitted, then rebelled again.

sentences.zh: 詔以同為幽州刺史兼尚書行台，同屢為德興所敗而還。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Tong as Youzhou Governor and concurrent Mobile Corps of the Secretariat; Tong was repeatedly defeated by Dexing and returned.
translations.idiomatic: By edict Lu Tong was made Governor of Youzhou and concurrently head of the Secretariat Mobile Corps; he was defeated repeatedly by Dexing and driven back.

sentences.zh: 魏朔方胡反，圍夏州刺史源子雍，城中食盡，煮馬皮而食之，眾無貳心。

translations.literal: Wei Shuofang Hu rebelled and besieged Xiazhou Governor Yuan Ziyong; food in the city was exhausted—they boiled horse hides to eat—yet the multitude had no divided loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: The Hu of Shuofang rebelled and besieged Yuan Ziyong, Governor of Xiazhou. When provisions ran out, the garrison boiled horse hides for food, yet none wavered in loyalty.

sentences.zh: 子雍欲自出求糧，留其子延伯守統萬，將佐皆曰：「今四方離叛，糧盡援絕，不若父子俱去。

translations.literal: Ziyong wished to go out himself to seek grain, leaving his son Yanbo to guard Tongwan; the officers all said, "Now the four quarters are in rebellion, grain is exhausted and reinforcements cut off—better that father and son both leave.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyong planned to go out himself for supplies, leaving his son Yanbo to hold Tongwan. His officers said, "The realm is in rebellion on every side; food is gone and aid will not come. Better that father and son flee together.

sentences.zh: 」子雍泣曰：「吾世荷國恩，當畢命此城；

translations.literal: Ziyong wept and said, "My family has long borne the state's grace; I ought to give my life entirely at this city;
translations.idiomatic: Ziyong wept and said, "My house has long enjoyed the state's favor; I am bound to die defending this city.

sentences.zh: 但無食可守，故欲往東州，為諸君營數月之食，若幸而得之，保全必矣。

translations.literal: But without food it cannot be held—therefore I wish to go to Eastern Xiazhou to procure months of provisions for you all; if by fortune I obtain them, preservation is assured.
translations.idiomatic: But with no food we cannot hold it. I mean to go to Eastern Xiazhou and gather provisions for you—for months, if need be. If fortune favors us, the city will surely be saved.

sentences.zh: 」乃師羸弱詣東夏州運糧，延伯與將佐哭而送之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he led the weak to Eastern Xiazhou to transport grain; Yanbo and the officers wept as they sent him off.
translations.idiomatic: He then took the weakened troops to Eastern Xiazhou to fetch grain; Yanbo and the officers wept as they saw him depart.

sentences.zh: 子雍行數日，胡帥曹阿各拔邀擊，擒之。

translations.literal: After Ziyong had marched several days, Hu chieftain Cao A-ge-ba intercepted and attacked, capturing him.
translations.idiomatic: Several days into the march, the Hu chieftain Cao A-ge-ba waylaid him and took him captive.

sentences.zh: 子雍潛遣人繼書，敕城中努力固守。

translations.literal: Ziyong secretly sent a messenger with a follow-up letter, instructing the city to strive to hold firm.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyong secretly sent word ahead, commanding the city to hold fast with all its strength.

sentences.zh: 闔城憂懼，延伯諭之曰：「吾父吉凶不可知，方寸焦爛。

translations.literal: The whole city was worried and afraid; Yanbo addressed them: "My father's fortune and misfortune cannot be known; my heart is scorched within an inch.
translations.idiomatic: The whole city was gripped with fear. Yanbo addressed them: "Whether my father lives or dies I cannot know; my heart burns within me.

sentences.zh: 但奉命守城，所為者重，不敢以私害公。

translations.literal: But receiving orders to defend the city, what I do is weighty—I dare not let private matters harm the public cause.
translations.idiomatic: Yet I have orders to hold this city—a weighty charge—and I dare not let private grief betray the public trust.

sentences.zh: 諸君幸得此心！

translations.literal: You all, may you attain this same heart!
translations.idiomatic: I pray you all share this resolve!

sentences.zh: 」於是眾感其義，莫不奮勵。

translations.literal: Thereupon the multitude was moved by his righteousness; none failed to rouse themselves with zeal.
translations.idiomatic: At this all were moved by his loyalty, and every man redoubled his efforts.

sentences.zh: 子雍雖被擒，胡人常以民禮事之，子雍為陳禍福，勸阿各拔降。

translations.literal: Though Ziyong was captured, the Hu always treated him with the rites due a civilian; Ziyong set forth fortune and calamity for them and urged A-ge-ba to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Though captive, the Hu treated Ziyong with civility. He spoke to them of gain and ruin and urged A-ge-ba to submit.

sentences.zh: 會阿各拔卒，其弟桑生竟帥其眾隨子雍降。

translations.literal: When A-ge-ba happened to die, his younger brother Sang Sheng ultimately led his followers to follow Ziyong in surrender.
translations.idiomatic: When A-ge-ba died, his brother Sang Sheng at last led the tribe to surrender with Ziyong.

sentences.zh: 子雍見行台北海王顥，具陳諸賊可滅之狀，顥給子雍兵，令其先驅。

translations.literal: Ziyong saw Mobile Corps Beihai Prince Hao and fully explained how the various rebels could be destroyed; Hao supplied Ziyong with troops and ordered him to advance as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyong presented himself to Prince Hao of Beihai, head of the Mobile Corps, and laid out how the rebels might be destroyed. Hao gave him troops and sent him ahead as vanguard.

sentences.zh: 時東夏州闔境皆反，所在屯結，子雍轉斗而前，九旬之中，凡數十戰，遂平東夏州，徵稅粟以饋統萬，二夏由是獲全。

translations.literal: At the time the whole territory of Eastern Xiazhou rebelled, with encampments everywhere; Ziyong fought turning battles forward; within ninety days, altogether several tens of battles—he then pacified Eastern Xiazhou, levied grain to supply Tongwan, and both Xia regions were thereby preserved whole.
translations.idiomatic: All Eastern Xiazhou had risen in revolt, rebels encamped everywhere. Ziyong fought his way forward through dozens of battles in ninety days, pacified the province, levied grain for Tongwan, and thus both Xia regions were saved.

sentences.zh: 子雍，懷之子也。

translations.literal: Ziyong was the son of Huai.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyong was a son of Huai.

sentences.zh: 魏廣陽王深上言：「今六鎮盡叛，高車二部亦與之同，以此疲兵擊之，必無勝理。

translations.literal: Wei Prince of Guangyang Shen memorialized: "Now the Six Garrisons have all rebelled, and the two divisions of Gaoche join them—with such weary troops to strike them, there is surely no principle of victory.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Shen of Guangyang memorialized: "The Six Garrisons have all rebelled, and the two Gaoche divisions stand with them. To strike with our exhausted army is to embrace certain defeat.

sentences.zh: 不若選練精兵守恆州諸要，更為後圖。

translations.literal: Better to select and drill elite troops to guard the key points of Hengzhou and plan afresh afterward.
translations.idiomatic: Better to choose and train fresh troops to hold Hengzhou's vital passes, and plan our next move from there.

sentences.zh: 」遂與李崇引兵還平城。

translations.literal: Thereupon he and Li Chong led troops back to Pingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: He and Li Chong then withdrew their army to Pingcheng.

sentences.zh: 崇謂諸將曰：「雲中者，白道之沖，賊之咽喉，若此地不全，則並、肆危矣。

translations.literal: Chong said to the generals: "Yunzhong is the chokepoint of the White Road, the throat of the rebels—if this place is not secured, then Bing and Si will be endangered.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chong told his generals, "Yunzhong guards the White Road—it is the rebels' jugular. If we lose it, Bing and Si will be imperiled.

sentences.zh: 當留一人鎮之，誰可者？

translations.literal: One must be left to garrison it—who will suffice?
translations.idiomatic: We must leave someone to hold it. Who is fit for the task?

sentences.zh: 」眾舉費穆，崇乃請穆為朔州刺史。

translations.literal: The assembly nominated Fei Mu; Chong then requested Mu as Governor of Shuozhou.
translations.idiomatic: The officers named Fei Mu, and Chong accordingly recommended him as Governor of Shuozhou.

sentences.zh: 賀拔度拔父子及武川宇文肱糾合鄉里豪傑，共襲衛可孤，殺之；

translations.literal: Helaba Dubo, father and son, and Wuchuan Yuwen Gu jointly rallied local heroes of the countryside, together assaulted Wei Ke'gu, and killed him;
translations.idiomatic: Helaba Dubo and his son, together with Yuwen Gu of Wuchuan, rallied local champions, attacked Wei Ke'gu, and killed him.

sentences.zh: 度拔尋與鐵勒戰死。

translations.literal: Dubo soon died in battle against the Tiele.
translations.idiomatic: Dubo soon fell fighting the Tiele.

sentences.zh: 肱，逸豆歸之玄孫也。

translations.literal: Gu was the great-grandson of Yidougui.
translations.idiomatic: Gu was a great-grandson of Yidougui.

sentences.zh: 李崇引國子博士祖瑩為長史；

translations.literal: Li Chong brought in Doctor of the Imperial Academy Zu Ying as Chief Clerk;
translations.idiomatic: Li Chong appointed Zu Ying, Doctor of the Imperial Academy, as his chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 廣陽王深奏瑩詐增首級，盜沒軍資，瑩坐除名，崇亦免官削爵征還。

translations.literal: Prince of Guangyang Shen memorialized that Ying fraudulently inflated head counts and embezzled military supplies; Ying was dismissed and struck from the rolls; Chong was also removed from office, stripped of rank, and recalled.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Shen of Guangyang accused Zu Ying of inflating enemy casualties and embezzling military stores. Ying was dismissed and struck from the rolls; Chong was also stripped of office and rank and recalled.

sentences.zh: 深專總軍政。

translations.literal: Shen alone held overall military and civil authority.
translations.idiomatic: Shen assumed sole command of military and civil affairs.

sentences.zh: 莫折天生進攻魏歧州，十一月，戊申，陷之，執都督元志及刺史裴芬之，送莫折念生，殺之。

translations.literal: Moqi Tiansheng advanced to attack Wei's Qizhou; in the eleventh month, on wushen, he captured it, seized Commander Yuan Zhi and Governor Pei Fenzhi, sent them to Moqi Niansheng, and killed them.
translations.idiomatic: Moqi Tiansheng marched on Qizhou. In the eleventh month, on wushen, he took the city, seized Commander Yuan Zhi and Governor Pei Fenzhi, sent them to Moqi Niansheng, and had them executed.

sentences.zh: 念生又使卜胡等寇涇州，敗光祿大夫薛巒於平涼東。

translations.literal: Niansheng again sent Bu Hu and others to raid Jingzhou, defeating Grand Master for Splendid Happiness Xue Luan east of Pingliang.
translations.idiomatic: Niansheng dispatched Bu Hu and others against Jingzhou and defeated Grand Master for Splendid Happiness Xue Luan east of Pingliang.

sentences.zh: 巒，安都之孫也。

translations.literal: Luan was the grandson of Andu.
translations.idiomatic: Luan was a grandson of Andu.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，彭寶孫拔魏東莞。

translations.literal: On bingchen, Peng Baosun captured Wei's Dongguan.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen, Peng Baosun took Dongguan from Wei.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，裴邃攻壽陽之安城，丙寅，馬頭、安城皆降。

translations.literal: On renxu, Pei Sui attacked Ancheng of Shouyang; on bingyin, Matou and Ancheng both surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu, Pei Sui assailed Ancheng near Shouyang; on bingyin, both Matou and Ancheng submitted.

sentences.zh: 高平人攻殺卜胡，共迎胡琛。

translations.literal: Men of Gaoping attacked and killed Bu Hu, jointly welcoming Hu Chen.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Gaoping killed Bu Hu and welcomed Hu Chen together.

sentences.zh: 魏以黃門侍郎楊昱兼侍中，持節監北海王顥軍，以救豳州，豳州圍解。

translations.literal: Wei appointed Yellow Gate Attendant Yang Yu concurrently Palace Attendant, with imperial credentials to oversee Beihai Prince Hao's army, to rescue Binzhou—the siege of Binzhou was lifted.
translations.idiomatic: Wei made Yellow Gate Attendant Yang Yu concurrent Palace Attendant and sent him with imperial commission to oversee Prince Hao of Beihai's army in relief of Binzhou; the siege was raised.

sentences.zh: 蜀賊張映龍、姜神達攻雍州，雍州刺史元修義請援，一日一夜，書移九通。

translations.literal: Shu rebels Zhang Yinglong and Jiang Shenda attacked Yongzhou; Yongzhou Governor Yuan Xiuyi requested reinforcements—within one day and one night, nine dispatches.
translations.idiomatic: The Shu rebels Zhang Yinglong and Jiang Shenda attacked Yongzhou. Governor Yuan Xiuyi pleaded for aid—nine dispatches in a single day and night.

sentences.zh: 都督李叔仁遲疑不赴，昱曰：「長安，關中基本，若長安不守，大軍自然瓦散，留此何益？

translations.literal: Commander Li Shuren hesitated and did not go; Yu said, "Chang'an is the foundation of Guanzhong—if Chang'an is not held, the great army will naturally scatter like tiles—what use in remaining here?
translations.idiomatic: Commander Li Shuren hung back and would not march. Yu said, "Chang'an is the root of Guanzhong. If Chang'an falls, the whole army will crumble—what good is staying here?

sentences.zh: 」遂與叔仁進擊之，斬神達，餘黨散走。

translations.literal: Thereupon together with Shuren he advanced to attack them, beheaded Shenda, and the remaining bandits scattered and fled.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed Shuren forward; they struck, beheaded Shenda, and the remnant rebels fled.

sentences.zh: 十二月，戊寅，魏荊山降。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on wuyin, Wei's Jingshan surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on wuyin, Jingshan submitted to Wei.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，魏以京兆王繼為太師、大將軍，都督西道諸軍以討莫折念生。

translations.literal: On renchen, Wei appointed Prince of Jingzhao Ji as Grand Preceptor, Grand General, Commander of all Western Route armies to campaign against Moqi Niansheng.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen, Wei made Prince Ji of Jingzhao Grand Preceptor and Grand General, Commander of all Western Route armies, to subdue Moqi Niansheng.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，武勇將軍李國興攻魏平靜關；

translations.literal: On yisi, General of Martial Courage Li Guoxing attacked Wei's Pingjing Pass;
translations.idiomatic: On yisi, General of Martial Courage Li Guoxing attacked Pingjing Pass;

sentences.zh: 辛丑，信威長史楊乾攻武陽關；

translations.literal: On xinchou, Chief Clerk of Trustworthy Prestige Yang Qian attacked Wuyang Pass;
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou, Chief Clerk of Trustworthy Prestige Yang Qian assailed Wuyang Pass;

sentences.zh: 任寅，攻峴關；

translations.literal: On renyin, [they] attacked Xian Pass;
translations.idiomatic: On renyin, they attacked Xian Pass;

sentences.zh: 皆克之。

translations.literal: All were captured.
translations.idiomatic: All were taken.

sentences.zh: 國興進圍郢州，魏郢州刺史裴詢與蠻酋西郢州刺史田樸特，相表裡以拒之。

translations.literal: Guoxing advanced to besiege Yingzhou; Wei Yingzhou Governor Pei Xun and barbarian chieftain Western Yingzhou Governor Tian Putie resisted in mutual coordination from within and without.
translations.idiomatic: Guoxing advanced to besiege Yingzhou. Pei Xun, Wei's Governor of Yingzhou, and the barbarian chieftain Tian Putie, Western Governor of Yingzhou, coordinated inside and out to resist.

sentences.zh: 圍城近百日，魏援軍至，國興引還。

translations.literal: The siege lasted nearly a hundred days; Wei relief troops arrived; Guoxing withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The siege lasted nearly a hundred days. When Wei relief arrived, Guoxing withdrew.

sentences.zh: 詢，駿之孫也。

translations.literal: Xun was the grandson of Jun.
translations.idiomatic: Xun was a grandson of Jun.

sentences.zh: 魏汾州諸胡反；

translations.literal: Various Hu of Wei Fenzhou rebelled;
translations.idiomatic: The Hu peoples of Fenzhou rebelled;

sentences.zh: 以章武王融為大都督，將兵討之。

translations.literal: Prince of Zhangwu Rong was made Grand Commander, leading troops to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Rong of Zhangwu was appointed Grand Commander and marched against them.

sentences.zh: 魏魏子建招諭南秦諸氐，稍稍降附，遂復六郡十二戍，斬賊帥韓祖香。

translations.literal: Wei Zijian of Wei summoned and persuaded the various Di of Southern Qin; they gradually submitted; he then recovered six commanderies and twelve garrisons, and beheaded rebel chieftain Han Zuxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zijian persuaded the Di of Southern Qin to submit one by one, recovered six commanderies and twelve garrisons, and beheaded the rebel leader Han Zuxiang.

sentences.zh: 魏以子建兼尚書，為行台，刺史如故，梁、巴、二益、二秦諸州皆受節度。

translations.literal: Wei appointed Zijian concurrently Director of the Secretariat, as Mobile Corps, Governor as before; the provinces of Liang, Ba, the two Yis, and the two Qins all received his command.
translations.idiomatic: Wei made Zijian concurrent Director of the Secretariat and head of a Mobile Corps, retaining his governorship; the provinces of Liang, Ba, the two Yis, and the two Qins all fell under his authority.

sentences.zh: 莫折念生遣兵攻涼州，城民趙天安復執刺史以應之。

translations.literal: Moqi Niansheng sent troops to attack Liangzhou; city resident Zhao Tian'an again seized the Governor to respond to him.
translations.idiomatic: Moqi Niansheng sent troops against Liangzhou; the townsman Zhao Tian'an once again seized the governor to join him.

sentences.zh: 是歲，侍中、太子詹事周捨坐事免，散騎常侍錢唐朱異代掌機密，軍旅謀議，方鎮改易，朝儀詔敕，皆典之。

translations.literal: That year, Palace Attendant and Household Steward of the Heir Apparent Zhou She was dismissed for an offense; Regular Palace Attendant of Qiantang Zhu Yi replaced him in managing secrets—military counsel, changes in frontier posts, court ritual and edicts, all were in his charge.
translations.idiomatic: That year Palace Attendant and Steward of the Heir Apparent Zhou She was dismissed for misconduct; Zhu Yi of Qiantang, Regular Palace Attendant, took over the confidential portfolios—military planning, frontier appointments, court ceremony, and imperial edicts—all passed through his hands.

sentences.zh: 異好文義，多藝能，精力敏贍，上以是任之。

translations.literal: Yi loved literary principles, had many talents, was energetic and quick in provision—the Emperor therefore entrusted him.
translations.idiomatic: Yi delighted in letters and learning, possessed many skills, and was tireless and keen—therefore the Emperor relied on him.

sentences.zh: 高祖武皇帝六普通六年（

translations.literal: Emperor Wu, Gaozu, sixth year of Putong (
translations.idiomatic: The sixth year of Putong of Emperor Wu, the Gaozu (

sentences.zh: 乙巳，公元五二五年）

translations.literal: yisi, AD 525)
translations.idiomatic: yisi, the year 525 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，丙午，雍州刺史晉安王綱遣安北長史柳渾破魏南鄉郡；

translations.literal: Spring, first month, on bingwu, Yongzhou Governor Prince of Jin'an Gang sent Chief Clerk of Pacifying the North Liu Hun to defeat Wei's Nanxiang Commandery;
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on bingwu, Prince Gang of Jin'an, Governor of Yongzhou, sent Liu Hun, Chief Clerk of Pacifying the North, to defeat Nanxiang Commandery.

sentences.zh: 司馬董當門破魏晉城，庚戌，又破馬圈、雕陽二城。

translations.literal: Major Dong Dangmen defeated Wei's Jincheng; on gengxu, he again defeated the two cities of Maquan and Diaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Major Dong Dangmen took Jincheng from Wei; on gengxu he also captured Maquan and Diaoyang.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，上祀南郊，大赦。

translations.literal: On xinhai, the Emperor sacrificed at the Southern Altar and proclaimed a great amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai, the Emperor offered sacrifice at the Southern Altar and proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 魏徐州刺史元法僧，素附元義，見義驕恣，恐禍及己，遂謀反。

translations.literal: Wei Xuzhou Governor Yuan Faseng had long attached himself to Yuan Yi; seeing Yi's arrogance and license, he feared calamity would reach himself, and therefore plotted rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Faseng, Wei's Governor of Xuzhou, had long sided with Yuan Yi. Seeing Yi's arrogance and excess, he feared he would be dragged down with him and plotted rebellion.

sentences.zh: 魏遺中書舍人張文伯至彭城，法僧謂曰：「吾欲與汝去危就安，能從我乎？

translations.literal: Wei sent Secretariat Aide Zhang Wenbo to Pengcheng. Faseng said to him, "I wish to go with you from danger to safety—can you follow me?
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Wei court sent Zhang Wenbo, an aide in the Secretariat, to Pengcheng. Yuan Faseng told him, "I want to leave peril for safety with you—will you come with me?"

sentences.zh: 」文伯曰：「我寧死見文陵松柏，安能去忠義而從叛逆乎！

translations.literal: " Wenbo said, "I would rather die and see the pines and cypresses at Wenling—how could I abandon loyalty and righteousness to follow a rebel!
translations.idiomatic: " Wenbo replied, "I would rather die and look once more upon the pines and cypresses at Wenling than forsake loyalty and follow a traitor!"

sentences.zh: 」法僧殺之。

translations.literal: " Faseng killed him.
translations.idiomatic: " Faseng had him put to death."

sentences.zh: 庚申，法僧殺行台高諒，稱帝，改元天啟，立諸子為王。

translations.literal: On gengshen, Faseng killed Commissioner Gao Liang, declared himself emperor, changed the era name to Tianqi, and enfeoffed his sons as kings.
translations.idiomatic: On the day gengshen, Faseng killed the commissioner Gao Liang, took the imperial title, proclaimed the era Tianqi, and made his sons princes."

sentences.zh: 魏發兵擊之，法僧乃遣其子景仲來降。

translations.literal: Wei sent troops to attack him; Faseng then sent his son Jingzhong to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Wei mobilized an army against him, whereupon Faseng sent his son Jingzhong to submit."

sentences.zh: 安東長史元顯和，麗之子也，舉兵與法僧戰；

translations.literal: Chief Clerk of Andong Yuan Xianhe, son of Li, raised troops and fought Faseng;
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Xianhe, chief clerk of Andong and a son of Yuan Li, took up arms against Faseng;"

sentences.zh: 法僧擒之，執其手，命其共坐，顯和不肯，曰：「與翁皆出皇家，一朝以地外叛，獨不畏良史乎！

translations.literal: Faseng captured him, took his hand, and ordered him to sit together; Xianhe refused and said, "You and I, old sir, both come from the imperial house—having rebelled with your territory in one morning, are you alone unafraid of the impartial historian!
translations.idiomatic: Faseng seized him, grasped his hand, and invited him to sit beside him. Xianhe refused and said, "We are both of the imperial clan, sir—yet you turned your province against the throne overnight. Do you not fear what the historians will write?"

sentences.zh: 」法僧猶欲慰諭之，顯和曰：「我寧死為忠鬼，不能生為叛臣！

translations.literal: " Faseng still wished to comfort and persuade him. Xianhe said, "I would rather die a loyal ghost than live as a disloyal minister!
translations.idiomatic: " Faseng tried still to reassure him. Xianhe said, "I would rather die a faithful ghost than live on as a rebel minister!"

sentences.zh: 」乃殺之。

translations.literal: " Then he was killed.
translations.idiomatic: " Faseng then executed him."

sentences.zh: 上使散騎常侍朱異使於法僧，以宣城太守元略為大都督，與將軍義興陳慶之、胡龍牙、成景俊等將兵應接。

translations.literal: The Emperor sent Regular Attendant Zhu Yi as envoy to Faseng, appointed Administrator of Xuancheng Yuan Lue as Grand Commander, and together with Generals Yixing Chen Qingzhi, Hu Longya, Cheng Jingjun, and others led troops to support him.
translations.idiomatic: The Liang emperor dispatched Zhu Yi as envoy to Faseng, named Yuan Lue, administrator of Xuancheng, grand commander, and sent him with the generals Chen Qingzhi of Yixing, Hu Longya, Cheng Jingjun, and others to reinforce Faseng with troops."

sentences.zh: 莫折天生軍於黑水，兵勢甚盛。

translations.literal: Moqi Tiansheng encamped his army at Heishui; his military strength was very formidable.
translations.idiomatic: Moqi Tiansheng had drawn up his forces at the Black Water, and his army was overwhelmingly strong."

sentences.zh: 魏以岐州刺史崔延伯為征西將軍、西道都督，帥眾五萬討之。

translations.literal: Wei appointed Cui Yanbo, Governor of Qizhou, as General Who Campaigns West and Commander of the Western Route, and he led fifty thousand men to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: Wei made Cui Yanbo, governor of Qizhou, general who campaigns west and western-route commander, and sent him with fifty thousand men to crush the rebels."

sentences.zh: 延伯與行台蕭寶寅軍於馬嵬。

translations.literal: Yanbo and Commissioner Xiao Baoyin encamped together at Mawei.
translations.idiomatic: Yanbo and the commissioner Xiao Baoyin camped together at Mawei."

sentences.zh: 延伯素驍勇，寶寅趣之使戰，延伯曰：「明晨為公參賊勇怯。

translations.literal: Yanbo had long been fierce and brave. Baoyin urged him to give battle. Yanbo said, "Tomorrow morning I will gauge for you the rebels' courage or cowardice.
translations.idiomatic: Yanbo was known for exceptional valor. Baoyin pressed him to fight. Yanbo said, "Tomorrow morning I will show you whether these rebels are bold or timid."

sentences.zh: 」乃選精兵數千西渡黑水，整陳進向天生營；

translations.literal: " He then selected several thousand elite troops to cross Heishui westward, arrayed his formations, and advanced toward Tiansheng's camp;
translations.idiomatic: " He chose several thousand picked soldiers, crossed the Black Water to the west, formed battle lines, and marched on Tiansheng's camp;"

sentences.zh: 寶寅軍於水東，遙為繼援。

translations.literal: Baoyin encamped east of the water and from afar served as rear support.
translations.idiomatic: Baoyin held the east bank of the river and stood ready to reinforce him from a distance."

sentences.zh: 延伯直抵天生營下，揚威脅之，徐引兵還。

translations.literal: Yanbo went straight to beneath Tiansheng's camp, displayed his might and threatened him, and slowly withdrew his troops.
translations.idiomatic: Yanbo rode straight to Tiansheng's camp, flaunted his power, then deliberately drew his men back."

sentences.zh: 天生見延伯眾少，開營爭逐之，其眾多於延伯十倍，蹙延伯於水次，寶寅望之失色。

translations.literal: Tiansheng saw that Yanbo's force was small; he opened camp and rushed in pursuit. His army was more than ten times Yanbo's and pressed Yanbo to the river's edge. Baoyin watched and turned pale.
translations.idiomatic: Tiansheng, seeing how few men Yanbo had, broke camp and gave chase. His host outnumbered Yanbo's by ten to one and drove him to the riverbank, while Baoyin looked on, his face drained of color."

sentences.zh: 延伯自為後殿，不與之戰，使其眾先渡，部伍嚴整，天生兵不敢擊。

translations.literal: Yanbo personally served as rearguard and did not engage them in battle, allowing his men to cross first. His ranks were strict and orderly; Tiansheng's troops dared not strike.
translations.idiomatic: Yanbo himself covered the retreat and refused to fight, letting his soldiers ford first. Their formation stayed tight and disciplined, and Tiansheng's men did not dare attack."

sentences.zh: 須臾，渡華，延伯徐渡，天生之眾亦引還。

translations.literal: After a short while, once the crossing was finished, Yanbo crossed slowly in turn, and Tiansheng's forces also withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: In a little while the crossing was done; Yanbo crossed at leisure, and Tiansheng's troops pulled back as well."

sentences.zh: 寶寅喜曰：「崔君之勇，關、張不如。

translations.literal: Baoyin said with delight, "Master Cui's bravery—Guan Yu and Zhang Fei were not his equal."
translations.idiomatic: Baoyin exclaimed with joy, "Commander Cui's courage puts even Guan Yu and Zhang Fei to shame."

sentences.zh: 」延伯曰：「此賊非老奴敵也，明公但安坐，觀老奴破之。

translations.literal: Yanbo said, "This bandit is no match for this old servant. My lord need only sit at ease and watch this old servant destroy him."
translations.idiomatic: Yanbo said, "This rebel is beneath an old soldier like me. Sit easy, my lord, and watch me break him."

sentences.zh: 」癸亥，延伯勒兵出，寶寅舉軍繼其後。

translations.literal: " On guihai, Yanbo marshaled his troops and went out; Baoyin led the whole army to follow behind him.
translations.idiomatic: " On guihai, Yanbo led his army out, and Baoyin followed with the full host."

sentences.zh: 天生悉眾逆戰，延伯身先士卒，陷其前鋒，將士盡銳競進，大破之，俘斬十餘萬，追奔至小隴，岐、雍及隴東皆平。

translations.literal: Tiansheng met him with his entire force in counterattack. Yanbo took the lead among the soldiers, broke through their vanguard, and officers and men alike pressed forward with full sharpness. He inflicted a great defeat, capturing and killing more than a hundred thousand, pursued the fugitives to Xiaolong, and Qi, Yong, and eastern Long were all pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Tiansheng came out with every man he had. Yanbo charged at the head of his troops, shattered the enemy van, and his officers and soldiers drove forward with all their might. The rebels were routed utterly—more than a hundred thousand killed or captured—and the pursuit ran to Xiaolong. Qizhou, Yongzhou, and eastern Long were all brought to order."

sentences.zh: 將士稽留采掠，天生遂塞隴道，由是諸軍不能進。

translations.literal: Officers and soldiers lingered to plunder and gather booty. Tiansheng thereupon blocked the Long road, and for this reason the various armies could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: The victorious troops halted to loot, and Tiansheng seized the chance to block the Long Pass road, so the government armies could advance no farther."

sentences.zh: 寶寅破宛川，俘其民以為奴婢，以美女十人賞岐州刺史魏蘭根，蘭根辭曰：「此縣介於強寇，不能自立，故附從以救死。

translations.literal: Baoyin captured Wanchuan and took its people captive as male and female servants. He rewarded Qizhou Governor Wei Langer with ten beautiful women. Langer declined, saying, "This county lies between powerful marauders and could not stand on its own; therefore its people attached themselves to survive death.
translations.idiomatic: Baoyin took Wanchuan and enslaved the population. He offered Wei Langer, governor of Qizhou, ten captive women as a reward. Langer refused, saying, "This district is caught between powerful raiders and could not survive alone; its people submitted only to stay alive."

sentences.zh: 官軍之至，宜矜而撫之，奈何助賊為虐，翦以為賤役乎！

translations.literal: " When the government army arrives, they ought to be pitied and soothed—how can you aid the bandits in their cruelty and cut them down into base servitude!
translations.idiomatic: " When our army comes, they deserve compassion and protection—why help the enemy torment them and reduce them to slaves?"

sentences.zh: 」悉求其父兄而歸之。

translations.literal: " He sought out all their fathers and elder brothers and sent them home.
translations.idiomatic: " He found every father and elder brother he could and sent them back to their families."

sentences.zh: 己巳，裴邃拔魏新蔡郡，詔侍中、領軍將軍西昌侯淵藻將眾前驅，南兗州刺史豫章王綜與諸將繼進。

translations.literal: On jisi, Pei Sui captured Wei's Xincai commandery. An edict ordered Palace Attendant and Director of the Guards, Marquis of Xichang Yuan Zao, to lead the troops as vanguard; the Prince of Yuzhang, Governor of Southern Yanzhou, Zong, and the various generals followed in advance.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi, Pei Sui seized Xincai commandery from Wei. The court ordered Palace Attendant and director of the guards Yuan Zao, Marquis of Xichang, to march ahead, while Prince Zong of Yuzhang, governor of southern Yanzhou, and the other generals followed."

sentences.zh: 癸酉，裴邃拔鄭城，汝、穎之間，所在響應。

translations.literal: On guiyou, Pei Sui captured Zheng city. Between the Ru and Ying rivers, everywhere responded in accord.
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou, Pei Sui took Zheng. Up and down the Ru and Ying valleys, cities rose in support."

sentences.zh: 魏河間王琛等憚邃威名，軍於城父，累月不進，魏朝遣廷尉少卿崔孝芬持節、繼齋庫刀以趣之。

translations.literal: Wei's Prince of Hejian, Chen, and others feared Sui's martial renown; they encamped at Chengfu and for many months did not advance. The Wei court sent Vice Minister of Justice Cui Xiaofen with credentials and the queued treasury sword to hasten them.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei princes Chen of Hejian and his colleagues feared Pei Sui's reputation; they sat at Chengfu and would not move for months. The Wei court dispatched Cui Xiaofen, vice minister of justice, bearing credentials and the imperial sword from the treasury to hurry them along."

sentences.zh: 孝芬，挺之子也。

translations.literal: Xiaofen was Ting's son.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaofen was the son of Cui Ting."

sentences.zh: 琛至壽陽，欲出兵決戰。

translations.literal: Chen reached Shouyang and wished to march out for a decisive battle.
translations.idiomatic: Chen arrived at Shouyang and wanted to march out for a pitched battle."

sentences.zh: 長孫稚以為久雨，未可出；

translations.literal: Changsun Zhi held that with prolonged rain it was not yet possible to go out;
translations.idiomatic: Changsun Zhi argued that the long rains made an sortie unwise;"

sentences.zh: 琛不聽，引兵五萬出城擊邃。

translations.literal: Chen would not listen; he led fifty thousand men out of the city to attack Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Chen would not heed him and led fifty thousand men from the city against Pei Sui."

sentences.zh: 邃為四甄以待之，使直閣將軍李祖憐先挑戰而偽退；

translations.literal: Sui formed four detachments to await them and had Regiment General Li Zulian first offer challenge and feign retreat;
translations.idiomatic: Pei Sui arrayed four wings to receive them and sent Regiment General Li Zulian to provoke a fight and then feign retreat;"

sentences.zh: 稚、琛悉眾追之，四甄競發，魏師大敗，斬首萬餘級。
