translations.literal: Zhi and Chen pursued with their entire force. The four detachments raced to strike together; the Wei army suffered a great defeat, with more than ten thousand heads cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi and Chen chased with their whole force. All four wings closed in at once; the Wei army was shattered, and more than ten thousand heads were taken."

sentences.zh: 琛走入城，稚勒兵而殿，遂閉門自固，不敢復出。

translations.literal: Chen ran into the city. Zhi marshaled the troops as rearguard and then shut the gates to hold firm, not daring to come out again.
translations.idiomatic: Chen fled back inside the walls. Zhi gathered the rear guard, then barred the gates and would not venture out again."

sentences.zh: 魏安樂王鑒將兵討元法僧，擊元略於彭城南。

translations.literal: Wei's Prince of Anle, Jian, led troops to suppress Yuan Faseng and attacked Yuan Lue south of Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Jian, prince of Anle, marched against Yuan Faseng and struck Yuan Lue south of Pengcheng."

sentences.zh: 略大敗，與數十騎走入城。

translations.literal: Lue suffered a great defeat and fled into the city with several dozen horsemen.
translations.idiomatic: Lue was routed and escaped into the city with only a few dozen horsemen."

sentences.zh: 鑒不設備，法僧出擊，大破之，鑒單騎奔歸。

translations.literal: Jian took no precautions. Faseng marched out and struck, inflicting a great defeat; Jian fled home alone on a single horse.
translations.idiomatic: Jian let his guard down. Faseng sallied forth, crushed him, and Jian rode off alone to safety."

sentences.zh: 將軍王希聃拔魏南陽平，執太守薛曇尚。

translations.literal: General Wang Xidan captured Wei's Nanyangping and seized Administrator Xue Tanshang.
translations.idiomatic: General Wang Xidan took Nanyangping from Wei and captured the administrator Xue Tanshang."

sentences.zh: 曇尚，虎子之子也。

translations.literal: Tanshang was Huzi's son.
translations.idiomatic: Tanshang was the son of Xue Huzi."

sentences.zh: 甲戌，以法僧為司空，封始安郡公。

translations.literal: On jiaxu, Faseng was appointed Minister of Works and enfeoffed as Duke of Shi'an commandery.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu, Faseng was named minister of works and created duke of Shi'an commandery."

sentences.zh: 魏以安豐王延明為東道行台，臨淮王彧為都督，以擊彭城。

translations.literal: Wei appointed Prince of Anfeng, Yanming, as Eastern Route Commissioner, and Prince of Linhuai, Yu, as Commander to attack Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Wei appointed Yuan Yanming, prince of Anfeng, eastern-route commissioner, and Yuan Yu, prince of Linhuai, commander, to retake Pengcheng."

sentences.zh: 魏以京兆王繼為太尉。

translations.literal: Wei appointed Prince of Jingzhao, Ji, as Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Wei named Yuan Ji, prince of Jingzhao, grand marshal."

sentences.zh: 二月，乙未，趙景悅拔魏龍亢。

translations.literal: Second month, on yiwei, Zhao Jingyue captured Wei's Longqiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on yiwei, Zhao Jingyue seized Longqiang from Wei."

sentences.zh: 初，魏劉騰既卒，胡太后及魏主左右防衛微緩。

translations.literal: Initially, after Liu Teng of Wei had died, Empress Dowager Hu and those around the Wei sovereign relaxed their guard somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, after Liu Teng's death, Empress Dowager Hu and the attendants around the Wei emperor loosened their watch."

sentences.zh: 元義亦自寬，時出遊於外，留連不返，其所親諫，義不納；

translations.literal: Yuan Yi also eased his own vigilance, often going out to roam abroad and lingering without returning. Those close to him remonstrated; Yi did not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Yi grew careless as well, often leaving the palace for outings and staying away. His intimates warned him, but he paid no heed."

sentences.zh: 太后察知之。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager observed and knew this.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager saw through it all."

sentences.zh: 去秋，太后對帝謂群臣曰：「今隔絕我母子，不聽往來，復何用我為！

translations.literal: The previous autumn, the Empress Dowager faced the Emperor and said to the assembled ministers, "Now they cut off me and my son and will not permit us to visit each other—of what further use am I!
translations.idiomatic: The previous autumn the empress dowager addressed the emperor before the court and said, "You keep my son and me apart and forbid us to meet—what good am I still?"

sentences.zh: 我當出家，修道於嵩山閒居寺耳。

translations.literal: " I shall leave family life and cultivate the Way at the Hermitage Temple on Mount Song."
translations.idiomatic: " I will take the tonsure and practice the Way at the Hermitage Temple on Mount Song."

sentences.zh: 」因欲自下發。

translations.literal: " She then wished to shave her own head.
translations.idiomatic: " She made as if to cut her own hair."

sentences.zh: 帝及群臣叩頭泣涕，殷勤苦請，太后聲色愈厲。

translations.literal: The Emperor and the assembled ministers knocked their heads and wept, earnestly and bitterly pleading. The Empress Dowager's voice and expression grew ever sterner.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor and the ministers kowtowed and wept, begging her again and again. The empress dowager only grew harsher in voice and face."

sentences.zh: 帝乃宿於嘉福殿，積數日，遂與太后密謀黜義。

translations.literal: The Emperor then lodged in the Hall of Blessed Fortune for several days and secretly plotted with the Empress Dowager to remove Yi.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor stayed several days in the Hall of Blessed Fortune and secretly plotted with the empress dowager to oust Yuan Yi."

sentences.zh: 然帝深匿形跡，太后有忿恚，欲得往來顯陽之言，皆以告義；

translations.literal: Yet the Emperor hid his tracks deeply. When the Empress Dowager was resentful and angry, wanting to visit and exchange words at Xianyang, he told Yi everything;
translations.idiomatic: Yet the emperor concealed his intentions carefully. Whenever the empress dowager grew angry and longed to visit him at Xianyang Palace, he reported every word to Yi;"

sentences.zh: 又對義流涕，敘太后欲出家，憂怖之心日有數四。

translations.literal: again he wept before Yi and recounted how the Empress Dowager wished to leave family life—his heart of worry and dread several times a day.
translations.idiomatic: he also wept before Yi, telling him the empress dowager meant to become a nun—his terror renewed itself three or four times a day."

sentences.zh: 義殊不以為疑，乃勸帝從太后所欲。

translations.literal: Yi was wholly without suspicion and thus urged the Emperor to follow what the Empress Dowager wished.
translations.idiomatic: Yi suspected nothing and urged the emperor to grant the empress dowager her wish."

sentences.zh: 於是太后數御顯陽殿，二宮無復禁礙。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Empress Dowager often went to the Hall of Manifest Sun; the two palaces were no longer barred.
translations.idiomatic: So the empress dowager began visiting Xianyang Hall often, and the two palaces were open to each other once more."

sentences.zh: 義舉元法僧為徐州，法僧反，太后數以為言，義深愧悔。

translations.literal: Yi had recommended Yuan Faseng for Xuzhou; Faseng rebelled. The Empress Dowager repeatedly brought this up in speech; Yi was deeply ashamed and regretful.
translations.idiomatic: Yi had put Yuan Faseng in charge of Xuzhou, and Faseng had rebelled. The empress dowager brought it up again and again until Yi was crushed with shame."

sentences.zh: 丞相高陽王雍，雖位居義上，而深畏憚之。

translations.literal: Chancellor Gao Yang, Prince of Gaoyang, though senior in rank to Yi, deeply feared him.
translations.idiomatic: The chancellor Yuan Yong, prince of Gaoyang, outranked Yi on paper yet feared him deeply."

sentences.zh: 會太后與帝游洛水，雍邀二宮幸其第。

translations.literal: It happened that the Empress Dowager and the Emperor were touring the Luo River. Yong invited the two palaces to visit his residence.
translations.idiomatic: When the empress dowager and emperor were enjoying the Luo River, Yong invited both palaces to his mansion."

sentences.zh: 日晏，帝與太后至雍內室，從者皆不得入，遂相與定圖義之計。

translations.literal: The day grew late. The Emperor and the Empress Dowager reached Yong's inner chamber; attendants were all barred from entering, and together they settled the plan to deal with Yi.
translations.idiomatic: As evening fell, the emperor and empress dowager entered Yong's private rooms alone; no attendants were admitted, and there they fixed the plan against Yi."

sentences.zh: 於是太后謂之曰：「元郎若忠於朝廷，無反心，何故不去領軍，以餘官輔政！

translations.literal: Thereupon the Empress Dowager said to him, "If Yuan-lang is loyal to the court and without rebel intent, why not relinquish command of the guards and assist in government with your remaining offices!
translations.idiomatic: Then the empress dowager said to Yi, "If you are true to the throne, Yuan, and harbor no treason, why not give up command of the guards and govern through your other posts?"

sentences.zh: 」義甚懼，免冠求解領軍。

translations.literal: " Yi was greatly afraid; he removed his cap and begged to be relieved of the guards command.
translations.idiomatic: " Yi was terrified; he took off his cap and begged to be relieved of the guards."

sentences.zh: 乃以義為驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司、尚書令、侍中、領左右。

translations.literal: He was then appointed Yi General of Agile Cavalry, with Privileges Equal to the Three Dukes, Director of the Department of State Affairs, Palace Attendant, and Commander of the Left and Right.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made general of agile cavalry with privileges equal to the three dukes, director of the Department of State Affairs, palace attendant, and commander of the left and right guards."

sentences.zh: 戊戌，魏大赦。

translations.literal: On wuxu, Wei proclaimed a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu, Wei declared a general amnesty."

sentences.zh: 壬辰，莫折念生遣都督楊鮓等攻仇池郡，行台魏子建擊破之。

translations.literal: On renchen, Moqi Niansheng sent Commander Yang Pan and others to attack Qiuichi commandery. Commissioner Wei Zijian defeated and routed them.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen, Moqi Niansheng sent the commander Yang Pan and others against Qiuichi commandery; Commissioner Wei Zijian beat them back."

sentences.zh: 三月，己酉，上幸白下城，履行六軍頓所。

translations.literal: Third month, on jiyou, the Emperor visited Baixia city and inspected the encampments of the Six Armies.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on jiyou, the emperor went to Baixia and reviewed the camps of the six armies."

sentences.zh: 乙丑，命豫章王綜權頓彭城，總督眾軍，並攝徐州府事。

translations.literal: On yichou, he ordered the Prince of Yuzhang, Zong, to provisionally encamp at Pengcheng, supervise all armies, and concurrently administer Xu Prefecture affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou, he ordered Prince Zong of Yuzhang to hold Pengcheng temporarily, command all forces, and oversee Xu province affairs."

sentences.zh: 己巳，以元法僧之子景隆為衡州刺史，景仲為廣州刺史。

translations.literal: On jisi, Faseng's son Jinglong was appointed governor of Hengzhou, and Jingzhong governor of Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi, Faseng's son Jinglong was made governor of Hengzhou and Jingzhong governor of Guangzhou."

sentences.zh: 上召法僧及元略還建康，法僧驅彭城吏民萬餘人南渡。

translations.literal: The Emperor summoned Faseng and Yuan Lue back to Jiankang. Faseng drove more than ten thousand officials and commoners of Pengcheng to cross south.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor recalled Faseng and Yuan Lue to Jiankang. Faseng herded more than ten thousand Pengcheng officials and commoners south across the river."

sentences.zh: 法僧至建康，上寵待甚厚；

translations.literal: When Faseng reached Jiankang, the Emperor favored and treated him very generously;
translations.idiomatic: When Faseng arrived in Jiankang, the emperor showered him with favor;"

sentences.zh: 元略惡其為人，與之言，未嘗笑。

translations.literal: Yuan Lue detested his character; in speaking with him he never once smiled.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Lue despised the man and never smiled in his company."

sentences.zh: 魏詔京光王繼班師。

translations.literal: Wei ordered Prince of Jingzhao Ji to withdraw the army.
translations.idiomatic: Wei ordered Yuan Ji, prince of Jingzhao, to withdraw his army."

sentences.zh: 北涼州刺史錫休儒等自魏興侵魏梁州，攻直城。

translations.literal: Governor of Northern Liangzhou Xi Xiu and others invaded Wei's Liangzhou from Weixing and attacked Zhicheng.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Xiu, governor of northern Liangzhou, and others crossed from Weixing into Wei's Liangzhou and attacked Zhicheng."

sentences.zh: 魏梁州刺史傅豎眼遣其子敬紹擊之，休儒等敗還。

translations.literal: Wei's Liangzhou governor Fu Shuyan sent his son Jingshao to attack them; Xiu and the others were defeated and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Shuyan, Wei's governor of Liangzhou, sent his son Jingshao against them; Xiu's force was beaten and retreated."

sentences.zh: 柔然王阿那瑰為魏討破六韓拔陵，魏遣牒雲具仁繼雜物勞賜之。

translations.literal: The Rouran king Anagui campaigned for Wei against Poliuhan Baling. Wei sent Dieyun Juren with supplies as gifts to reward and console him.
translations.idiomatic: The Rouran king Anagui fought Poliuhan Baling on Wei's behalf, and Wei sent Dieyun Juren with gifts and supplies to reward him."

sentences.zh: 阿那瑰勒眾十萬，自武川西向沃野，屢破拔陵兵。

translations.literal: Anagui marshaled a hundred thousand men, from Wuchuan west toward Woye, and repeatedly defeated Balang's troops.
translations.idiomatic: Anagui mustered a hundred thousand warriors, marched west from Wuchuan toward Woye, and repeatedly shattered Baling's army."

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，魏主復遣中書舍人馮俊勞賜阿那瑰。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, the Wei sovereign again sent Secretariat Aide Feng Jun to reward and console Anagui.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, the Wei emperor again sent the secretariat aide Feng Jun with rewards for Anagui."

sentences.zh: 阿那瑰部落浸強，自稱敕連頭兵豆伐可汗。

translations.literal: Anagui's tribes gradually grew strong; he styled himself Chiliantoubing Doufa Khan.
translations.idiomatic: Anagui's tribes grew ever stronger, and he proclaimed himself khan under the title Chiliantoubing Doufa."

sentences.zh: 魏元義雖解兵權，猶總任內外，殊不自意有廢黜之理。

translations.literal: Yuan Yi of Wei, though he had relinquished military authority, still held overall charge within and without, and by no means imagined there was reason to depose him.
translations.idiomatic: Though Yuan Yi had surrendered military command, he still controlled affairs inside and outside the court and never dreamed he could be cast down."

sentences.zh: 胡太后意猶豫未決，侍中穆紹勸太后速去之。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Hu's mind still hesitated, undecided. Palace Attendant Mu Shao urged the Empress Dowager to remove him quickly.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Hu still wavered. Palace Attendant Mu Shao urged her to act against Yi at once."

sentences.zh: 紹，亮之子也。

translations.literal: Shao was Liang's son.
translations.idiomatic: Shao was the son of Mu Liang."

sentences.zh: 潘嬪有寵於魏主，宦官張景嵩說之云：「義欲害嬪。

translations.literal: Consort Pan had the Wei sovereign's favor. Eunuch Zhang Jingsong said to her, "Yi wishes to harm the Consort."
translations.idiomatic: Consort Pan held the Wei emperor's affection. The eunuch Zhang Jingsong told her, "Yuan Yi means to destroy you."

sentences.zh: 」嬪泣訴於帝曰：「義非獨欲殺妾，又將不利於陛下。

translations.literal: " The Consort wept and appealed to the Emperor, "Yi does not only wish to kill your servant—he also intends harm to Your Majesty."
translations.idiomatic: " She wept before the emperor and said, "Yi wants not only my life—he plots against Your Majesty as well."

sentences.zh: 」帝信之，因義出宿，解義侍中。

translations.literal: " The Emperor believed her. When Yi went out to lodge overnight, he removed Yi from Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor believed her. The night Yi stayed outside the palace, he stripped him of the post of palace attendant."

sentences.zh: 明旦，義將入宮，門者不納。

translations.literal: The next dawn, when Yi was about to enter the palace, the gatekeepers would not admit him.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn the next day, when Yi tried to enter the palace, the guards turned him away."

sentences.zh: 辛卯，太后復臨朝攝政，下詔追削劉騰官爵，除義名為民。

translations.literal: On xinmao, the Empress Dowager again attended court and held regency. An edict was issued posthumously stripping Liu Teng of office and rank, and Yuan Yi was removed from the registers and made a commoner.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao the empress dowager resumed regency at court. An edict posthumously erased Liu Teng's titles, and Yuan Yi was struck from the rolls and reduced to commoner status."

sentences.zh: 清河國郎中令韓子熙上書為清河王懌訟冤，乞誅元義等，曰：「昔趙高柄秦，令關東鼎沸；

translations.literal: Chief of the Prince of Qinghe's household, Han Zixi, submitted a memorial pleading the injustice done to Prince Qinghe, Yi, and begging execution of Yuan Yi and others. He said, "In former times Zhao Gao held Qin's reins and made the lands east of the passes boil like a cauldron;
translations.idiomatic: Han Zixi, chief of the household of the prince of Qinghe, submitted a memorial vindicating Prince Qinghe, Yuan Yi, and demanding the execution of Yuan Yi and his allies. He wrote, "Once Zhao Gao seized Qin and set the east ablaze;"

sentences.zh: 今元義專魏，使四方雲擾。

translations.literal: now Yuan Yi monopolizes Wei and throws the four quarters into tumult like storm clouds.
translations.idiomatic: now Yuan Yi dominates Wei and throws the realm into chaos."

sentences.zh: 開逆之端，起於宋維，成禍之末，良由劉騰，宜梟首洿宮，斬骸沉族，以明其罪。

translations.literal: " The beginning of rebellion was raised by Song Wei; the completion of disaster was truly due to Liu Teng—they ought to have their heads displayed at the polluted palace and their corpses cut down and their clans drowned, to clarify their crime."
translations.idiomatic: " Song Wei opened the road to treason; Liu Teng brought the catastrophe to fruition. Their heads should hang at the palace gate, their bodies destroyed and their clans wiped out, that all may see their guilt."

sentences.zh: 」太后命發劉騰之墓，露散其骨，籍沒家貲，盡殺其養子。

translations.literal: " The Empress Dowager ordered Liu Teng's tomb opened, his bones exposed and scattered, his household property confiscated, and all his adopted sons killed.
translations.idiomatic: " The empress dowager had Liu Teng's tomb opened, his bones cast out, his property seized, and every adopted son executed."

sentences.zh: 以子熙為中書舍人。

translations.literal: Zixi was appointed Secretariat Aide.
translations.idiomatic: Zixi was appointed secretariat aide."

sentences.zh: 子熙，麒麟之孫也。

translations.literal: Zixi was Qilin's grandson.
translations.idiomatic: Zixi was a grandson of Han Qilin."

sentences.zh: 初，宋維父弁常曰：「維性疏險，必敗吾家！

translations.literal: Initially, Song Wei's father Bian often said, "Wei is coarse by nature and perilous—he will surely ruin our house!
translations.idiomatic: Long before, Song Wei's father Bian had said, "That boy is reckless and dangerous—he will destroy our family!"

sentences.zh: 」李崇、郭祚、游肇亦曰：「伯緒凶疏，終傾宋氏。

translations.literal: " Li Chong, Guo Zuo, and You Zhao also said, "Boxu's fierceness and heedlessness will in the end overturn the Song clan.
translations.idiomatic: " Li Chong, Guo Zuo, and You Zhao likewise said, "Boxu is brutal and rash—the Song house will fall because of him."

sentences.zh: 若得殺身，幸矣！

translations.literal: " If one could die in the body, it would be fortunate!
translations.idiomatic: " If he dies in the attempt, we may count ourselves lucky!"

sentences.zh: 」維阿附元義，超遷至洛州刺史，至是除名，尋賜死。

translations.literal: " Wei attached himself to Yuan Yi and was abruptly promoted to governor of Luozhou; at this time he was struck from the registers, and soon he was granted death.
translations.idiomatic: " Wei had curried favor with Yuan Yi and vaulted to governor of Luozhou; now he was erased from the registers and soon compelled to take his own life."

sentences.zh: 義之解領軍也，太后以義黨與尚強，未可猝制，乃以侯剛代義為領軍以安其意。

translations.literal: " When Yi relinquished command of the guards, the Empress Dowager, because Yi's faction was still strong and he could not be suddenly controlled, appointed Hou Gang to replace Yi as commander of the guards to set his mind at ease.
translations.idiomatic: " When Yi gave up the guards, the empress dowager—knowing his faction remained powerful and he could not be struck down abruptly—named Hou Gang commander of the guards in his place to lull him."

sentences.zh: 尋出剛為冀州刺史，加儀同三司，未至州，黜為征虜將軍，卒於家。

translations.literal: Soon Hou Gang was sent out as Governor of Jizhou, with privileges equal to the three dukes added; before he reached the province he was demoted to General Who Subdues the Barbarians and died at home.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Gang was soon appointed governor of Jizhou with privileges equal to the three dukes, but before he took up the post he was reduced to general who subdues the barbarians and died at home.

sentences.zh: 太后欲殺賈粲，以義黨多，恐驚動內外，乃出粲為濟州刺史，尋追殺之，籍沒其家。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager wished to kill Jia Can, but because Yi's faction was numerous she feared alarming those within and without; she therefore sent Can out as Governor of Jizhou and soon pursued and killed him, confiscating his household property.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager wanted Jia Can executed, yet Yi's allies were still many and she feared a shock inside and outside the court; she posted Can to Jizhou, then had him hunted down and killed and his estate seized.

sentences.zh: 唯義以妹夫，未忍行誅。

translations.literal: Only toward Yi, as her brother-in-law, did she not bear to carry out execution.
translations.idiomatic: Only Yuan Yi, as her brother-in-law, she could not bring herself to kill outright.

sentences.zh: 先是，給事黃門侍郎元順以剛直忤義意，以為齊州刺史；

translations.literal: Earlier, Attendant of the Yellow Gate Yuan Shun, for being upright and outspoken, had offended Yi's wishes and was appointed Governor of Qizhou;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Yuan Shun, an attendant at the yellow gate, had crossed Yuan Yi with his blunt honesty and was sent to govern Qizhou;

sentences.zh: 太后征還，為侍中。

translations.literal: the Empress Dowager recalled him and made him Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: the empress dowager recalled him and named him palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 侍坐於太后，義妻在太后側，順指之曰：「陛下奈何以一妹之故，不正元義之罪，使天下不得伸其冤憤！

translations.literal: Sitting in attendance before the Empress Dowager, with Yi's wife at the Empress Dowager's side, Shun pointed at her and said, "Your Majesty, how can you for the sake of one younger sister fail to rectify Yuan Yi's crimes and keep the realm from venting its grievance and rage!
translations.idiomatic: While attending the empress dowager, with Yi's wife beside her, Shun pointed and said, "For one sister's sake, Majesty, how can you leave Yuan Yi's crimes uncorrected and deny the empire its justice?"

sentences.zh: 」太后嘿然。

translations.literal: " The Empress Dowager was silent.
translations.idiomatic: " The empress dowager said nothing.

sentences.zh: 順，澄之子也。

translations.literal: Shun was Cheng's son.
translations.idiomatic: Shun was a son of Yuan Cheng.

sentences.zh: 它日，太后從容謂侍臣曰：「劉騰、元義昔邀朕求鐵券，冀得不死，朕賴不與。

translations.literal: Another day the Empress Dowager said casually to the attending ministers, "Liu Teng and Yuan Yi once begged me for iron certificates, hoping they would not die; I relied on not granting them."
translations.idiomatic: On another day the empress dowager remarked to her ministers, "Liu Teng and Yuan Yi once begged me for iron warrants so they might escape death; I refused."

sentences.zh: 」韓子熙曰：「事關生殺，豈系鐵券！

translations.literal: Han Zixi said, "Matters touch life and death—how could they depend on iron certificates!
translations.idiomatic: Han Zixi said, "Life and death are not settled by iron warrants!

sentences.zh: 且陛下昔雖不與，何解今日不殺！

translations.literal: " Moreover, though Your Majesty did not grant them then, why not kill them today!
translations.idiomatic: " And even if you withheld them then, why spare them now?"

sentences.zh: 」太后憮然。

translations.literal: " The Empress Dowager looked dismayed.
translations.idiomatic: " The empress dowager looked stricken.

sentences.zh: 未幾，有告義及弟瓜謀誘六鎮降戶反於定州，又招魯陽諸蠻侵擾伊闕，欲為內應。

translations.literal: Before long, someone reported that Yi and his younger brother Gua plotted to induce the surrendered households of the Six Garrisons to rebel at Dingzhou, and also recruited the various barbarians of Luyang to harass Yique, intending to serve as inside collaborators.
translations.idiomatic: Soon reports came that Yi and his brother Gua meant to stir the Six Garrisons settlers at Dingzhou to revolt and rouse the Luyang tribes against Yique as internal allies.

sentences.zh: 得其手書，太后猶未忍殺之。

translations.literal: When his own handwriting was obtained, the Empress Dowager still could not bear to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Even with his own letters in hand, the empress dowager still hesitated to kill him.

sentences.zh: 群臣固執不已，魏主亦以為言，太后乃從之，賜義及弟瓜死於家，猶贈義驃騎大將軍、儀同三司、尚書令。

translations.literal: The assembled ministers pressed unyieldingly. The Wei sovereign also spoke on the matter, and the Empress Dowager then consented, granting Yi and his younger brother Gua death at home; she still posthumously awarded Yi the titles General of Agile Cavalry, privileges equal to the three dukes, and Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers would not relent, and the Wei emperor spoke too; at last she agreed. Yi and Gua were allowed to die at home, though Yi was still honored posthumously as general of agile cavalry, with privileges equal to the three dukes, and director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 江陽王繼廢於家，病卒。

translations.literal: Prince of Jiangyang Ji was deposed and confined at home; he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Ji, prince of Jiangyang, was stripped of office and confined at home, where he died of illness.

sentences.zh: 前幽州刺史盧同坐義黨除名。

translations.literal: Former Governor of Youzhou Lu Tong was struck from the registers for belonging to Yi's faction.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Tong, former governor of Youzhou, was erased from the rolls as one of Yi's party.

sentences.zh: 太后頗事妝飾，數出遊幸，元順面諫曰：「《禮》，婦人夫沒自稱未亡人，首去珠玉，衣不文采。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager rather devoted herself to adornment and often went out on tours of pleasure. Yuan Shun remonstrated to her face, saying, "In the Rites, when a woman's husband dies she calls herself 'one who is not yet dead,' removes pearls and jade from her head, and wears no patterned garments.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager took to elaborate dress and frequent outings. Yuan Shun rebuked her openly: "The Rites say a widow calls herself 'not yet dead,' lays aside pearls and jade, and wears no finery.

sentences.zh: 陛下母臨天下，年垂不惑，修飾過甚，何以儀型後世！

translations.literal: " Your Majesty as mother overseeing the realm, your years nearing forty, yet your adornment excessive—how will you model yourself for later generations!
translations.idiomatic: " You rule the empire as mother, you are nearly forty, yet you adorn yourself beyond measure—what example is this for posterity?"

sentences.zh: 」太后慚而還宮，召順，責之曰：「千里相征，豈欲眾中見辱邪！

translations.literal: " The Empress Dowager, ashamed, returned to the palace, summoned Shun, and reproached him, saying, "I summoned you from a thousand li—was it to be humiliated before the assembly!
translations.idiomatic: " Ashamed, she returned to the palace, called Shun in, and scolded him: "I fetched you from afar—did I mean for you to shame me before everyone?"

sentences.zh: 」順曰：「陛下不畏天下之笑，而恥臣之一言乎！

translations.literal: " Shun said, "Your Majesty does not fear the world's laughter, yet is ashamed before one remark of your servant!
translations.idiomatic: " Shun said, "You do not fear the world's mockery, yet you blush at one word from me?"

sentences.zh: 順與穆紹同直，順因醉，入其寢所，紹擁被而起，正色讓順曰：「身二十年侍中，與卿先君亟連職事，縱卿方進用，何宜相排突也！

translations.literal: Shun and Mu Shao were on duty together. Shun, being drunk, entered his sleeping quarters. Shao threw off his covers and rose, sternly reproaching Shun: "I have been Palace Attendant for twenty years and served often with your late father in the same offices; though you are newly promoted, how can you barge in so rudely!
translations.idiomatic: Shun and Mu Shao shared a watch. Drunk, Shun walked into Shao's bedchamber. Shao threw off his quilt and stood, rebuking him: "Twenty years I have been palace attendant, often alongside your father—yet because you are newly favored you may storm in on me?"

sentences.zh: 」遂謝事還家，詔諭久之，乃起。

translations.literal: " He then resigned his post and returned home; an edict exhorted him for a long time before he resumed office.
translations.idiomatic: " He resigned and went home; only after long imperial pleading did he return to office.

sentences.zh: 初，鄭羲之兄孫儼為司徒胡國珍行參軍，私得幸於太后，人未之知。

translations.literal: Initially, Zheng Yi's elder brother's grandson Yan was a staff officer under Director of the Secretariat Hu Guozhen and in private won the Empress Dowager's favor, though no one knew it.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Zheng Yan, grandson of Zheng Yi's elder brother, served on the staff of the director of the Secretariat Hu Guozhen and secretly won the empress dowager's favor, though none knew it.

sentences.zh: 蕭寶寅西討，以儼為開府屬。

translations.literal: When Xiao Baoyin campaigned west, Yan was made a staff member of his headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Baoyin marched west, Yan was attached to his headquarters.

sentences.zh: 太后再攝政，儼請奉使還朝，太后留之，拜諫議大夫、中書舍人，領嘗食典御，晝夜禁中；

translations.literal: When the Empress Dowager again held regency, Yan asked to return on a mission; the Empress Dowager kept him, appointed him Remonstrating and Consulting Grandee and Secretariat Aide, and put him in charge of the imperial kitchen, day and night within the inner palace;
translations.idiomatic: When the empress dowager resumed regency, Yan asked to return on embassy; she kept him, made him remonstrating and consulting grandee and secretariat aide, and put him in charge of the imperial kitchen, living day and night in the inner palace;

sentences.zh: 每休沐，太后常遣宦者隨之，儼見其妻，唯得言家事而已。

translations.literal: whenever he had leave, the Empress Dowager always sent eunuchs to follow him; when Yan saw his wife he could speak only of household affairs.
translations.idiomatic: on his rare days off the empress dowager sent eunuchs to trail him; when he saw his wife he might discuss only domestic matters.

sentences.zh: 中書舍人樂安徐紇，粗有文學，先以謅事趙修，坐徙枹罕。

translations.literal: Secretariat Aide Xu He of Le'an had some literary ability; he had earlier curried favor with Zhao Xiu through flattery and was banished to Fuhan for it.
translations.idiomatic: Xu He of Le'an, a secretariat aide, had modest literary talent; he had once flattered Zhao Xiu and was exiled to Fuhan.

sentences.zh: 後還，復除中書舍人，又諂事清河王懌；

translations.literal: After returning he was again appointed Secretariat Aide and again flattered Prince of Qinghe Yi;
translations.idiomatic: Recalled, he again became secretariat aide and fawned on Prince Qinghe, Yuan Yi;

sentences.zh: 懌死，出為雁門太守。

translations.literal: when Yi died he was sent out as Governor of Yanmen.
translations.idiomatic: when Yi fell he was posted to Yanmen as governor.

sentences.zh: 還洛，復諂事元義。

translations.literal: Returning to Luoyang, he again flattered Yuan Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Back in Luoyang he curried favor with Yuan Yi once more.

sentences.zh: 義敗，太后以紇為懌所厚，復召為中書舍人，紇又諂事鄭儼。

translations.literal: When Yi fell, the Empress Dowager because He had been thick with Yi recalled him as Secretariat Aide; He again flattered Zheng Yan.
translations.idiomatic: After Yi's downfall the empress dowager, remembering He's closeness to Yi, recalled him as secretariat aide; He then attached himself to Zheng Yan.

sentences.zh: 儼以紇有智數，仗為謀主；

translations.literal: Yan because He had resourceful schemes relied on him as chief strategist;
translations.idiomatic: Yan, valuing He's cunning, made him his chief strategist;

sentences.zh: 紇以儼有內寵，傾身承接，共相表裡，勢傾內外，號為「徐鄭」。

translations.literal: He because Yan had inner favor threw himself into service; together they acted inside and outside, their power overwhelming court and capital, and they were called "Xu and Zheng."
translations.idiomatic: He, because Yan enjoyed inner favor, devoted himself utterly; together they ruled inside and out, and men spoke of "Xu and Zheng."

sentences.zh: 儼累遷至中書令、車騎將軍；

translations.literal: Yan was promoted in succession to Director of the Secretariat and General of Cavalry and Chariots;
translations.idiomatic: Yan rose to director of the Secretariat and general of cavalry and chariots;

sentences.zh: 紇累遷至給事黃門侍郎，仍領舍人，總攝中書、門下之事，軍國詔令莫不由之。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Attendant of the Yellow Gate, still holding the aide post, controlling altogether the affairs of the Secretariat and the Gate, so that no military or state edict or order did not pass through them.
translations.idiomatic: He became attendant at the yellow gate while retaining the aide post, controlling Secretariat and Gate business so that no military or state order passed without them.

sentences.zh: 紇有機辯強力，終日治事，略無休息，不以為勞。

translations.literal: He was quick-witted and forceful, handling affairs all day with scarcely a rest and not counting it labor.
translations.idiomatic: He was sharp-tongued and tireless, working from dawn to dusk without complaint.

sentences.zh: 時有急詔，令數吏執筆，或行或臣，人別佔之，造次俱成，不失事理。

translations.literal: When urgent edicts came, he had several clerks take brush—some standing, some kneeling, each assigned a portion—and on the spot all finished without losing sense or logic.
translations.idiomatic: Urgent orders might set several clerks writing at once, standing or kneeling, each taking a section; drafts appeared in moments, always coherent.

sentences.zh: 然無經國大體，專好小數，見人矯為恭謹，遠近輻湊附之。

translations.literal: Yet he had no grand vision for governing the state and specialized in petty tricks; seeing others affect deference, people near and far flocked to attach themselves to him.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he had no vision for statecraft and loved petty maneuvering; the obsequious crowded in from every quarter.

sentences.zh: 給事黃門侍郎袁翻、李神軌皆領中書舍人，為太后所信任，時人云神軌亦得幸於太后，眾莫能明也。

translations.literal: Attendants of the Yellow Gate Yuan Fan and Li Shengui both held Secretariat aide posts and were trusted by the Empress Dowager; people at the time said Shengui also won the Empress Dowager's favor, though none could be sure.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Fan and Li Shengui, attendants at the yellow gate, also served as secretariat aides and enjoyed the empress dowager's trust; rumor said Shengui shared her bed, though none could prove it.

sentences.zh: 神軌求婚於散騎常侍盧義僖，義僖不許。

translations.literal: Shengui sought marriage with Regular Attendant Lu Yixi; Yixi would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Shengui asked to marry into the family of Regular Attendant Lu Yixi; Yixi refused.

sentences.zh: 黃門侍郎王誦謂義僖曰：「昔人不以一女易眾男，卿豈易之邪！

translations.literal: Yellow Gate Attendant Wang Song said to Yixi, "Men of old would not trade one daughter for many sons—would you make such a trade!
translations.idiomatic: Yellow Gate Attendant Wang Song told Yixi, "Our forebears would not trade one daughter for a houseful of sons—would you?"

sentences.zh: 」義僖曰：「所以不從，正為此耳。

translations.literal: " Yixi said, "The reason I do not consent is precisely this.
translations.idiomatic: " Yixi said, "That is exactly why I refuse.

sentences.zh: 從之，恐禍大而速。

translations.literal: " If I consented, I fear disaster would be great and swift."
translations.idiomatic: " Consent, and ruin would come fast and hard."

sentences.zh: 」誦乃堅握義僖手曰：「我聞有命，不敢以告人。

translations.literal: Song then gripped Yixi's hand firmly and said, "I have heard there is a fate—I dare not tell another."
translations.idiomatic: Song seized Yixi's hand and said, "I have heard what fate holds—I dare not speak it aloud."

sentences.zh: 」女遂適他族。

translations.literal: The daughter was then married into another clan.
translations.idiomatic: The daughter was betrothed elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 臨婚之夕，太后遣中使宣敕停之，內外惶怖，義僖夷然自若。

translations.literal: On the eve of the wedding the Empress Dowager sent an inner envoy with an edict to halt it; inside and outside were terrified, yet Yixi remained calm and unperturbed.
translations.idiomatic: On the wedding eve the empress dowager sent an imperial messenger to stop the match; the household panicked, but Yixi stayed calm.

sentences.zh: 神軌，崇之子；

translations.literal: Shengui was Chong's son;
translations.idiomatic: Shengui was the son of Li Chong;

sentences.zh: 義僖，度世之孫也。

translations.literal: Yixi was Dushi's grandson.
translations.idiomatic: Yixi was a grandson of Lu Dushi.

sentences.zh: 胡琛據高平，遣其大將-{万俟}-丑奴、宿勤明達等寇魏涇州，將軍盧祖遷、伊甕生討之，不克。

translations.literal: Hu Chen held Gaoping and sent his great generals Wanqi Chounu, Su Qin Mingda, and others to raid Wei's Jingzhou; Generals Lu Zuqian and Yi Wengsheng attacked them but could not overcome them.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Chen held Gaoping and sent his generals Wanqi Chounu, Su Qin Mingda, and others against Wei's Jingzhou; Generals Lu Zuqian and Yi Wengsheng failed to break them.

sentences.zh: 蕭寶寅、崔延伯既破莫折天生，引兵會祖遷等於安定，甲卒十二萬，鐵馬八千，軍威甚盛。

translations.literal: Xiao Baoyin and Cui Yanbo, having already defeated Moqi Tiansheng, led their troops to join Zuqian and the others at Anding—one hundred twenty thousand armored soldiers and eight thousand iron horses, their military might very imposing.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Baoyin and Cui Yanbo, fresh from defeating Moqi Tiansheng, joined Zuqian at Anding with a hundred and twenty thousand men and eight thousand armored horses, a formidable host.

sentences.zh: 丑奴軍於安定西北七里，時以輕騎挑戰。

translations.literal: Chounu encamped seven li northwest of Anding and at the time used light cavalry to offer challenge.
translations.idiomatic: Chounu camped seven li northwest of Anding and probed with light cavalry.

sentences.zh: 大兵未交，輒委走。

translations.literal: Before the great armies clashed they would feign flight.
translations.idiomatic: Before the main forces met they would pretend to flee.

sentences.zh: 延伯恃其勇，且新有功，遂唱議為先驅擊之。

translations.literal: Yanbo relied on his bravery and on his recent merit and thus loudly proposed to lead the vanguard in striking them.
translations.idiomatic: Yanbo, proud of his valor and recent victory, volunteered to lead the van.

sentences.zh: 別造大盾，內為鎖柱，使壯士負而趨，謂之排城，置輜重於中，戰士在外，自安定北緣原北上。

translations.literal: They separately built great shields with iron pillars inside, having strong men bear them forward in a rush—called "pushing walls"—and placed baggage in the center with warriors outside, from north of Anding along the high ground marching north.
translations.idiomatic: They built huge shields braced with iron pillars, borne forward by strong men in a "pushing wall" formation, baggage in the center and fighters outside, marching north along the heights from Anding.

sentences.zh: 將戰，有賊數百騎詐持文書，雲是降簿，且乞緩師。

translations.literal: About to give battle, several hundred rebel horsemen falsely held documents, saying they were registers of surrender and begging a pause in the attack.
translations.idiomatic: As battle neared, hundreds of rebel horsemen waved papers claiming to be surrender rolls and begging for a halt.

sentences.zh: 寶寅、延伯未及閱視，宿勤明達引兵自東北至，降賊自西競下，覆背擊之。

translations.literal: Baoyin and Yanbo had not yet time to examine them when Su Qin Mingda led troops from the northeast and the surrendering rebels rushed down from the west, striking them from front and rear.
translations.idiomatic: Before Baoyin and Yanbo could read them, Su Qin Mingda struck from the northeast while the "surrender" party swept down from the west, hitting them front and back.

sentences.zh: 延伯上馬奮擊，逐北徑抵其營。

translations.literal: Yanbo mounted his horse and fought fiercely, pursuing north straight to their camp.
translations.idiomatic: Yanbo charged, driving the pursuit to the enemy camp.

sentences.zh: 賊皆輕騎，延伯軍雜步卒，戰久疲乏，賊乘間得入排城；

translations.literal: The rebels were all light cavalry; Yanbo's army mixed in foot soldiers. After long fighting they were weary; the rebels seized an opening and entered the pushing walls;
translations.idiomatic: The rebels were all light horse; Yanbo's ranks included foot soldiers. After long fighting his men tired, and the enemy broke into the pushing walls;

sentences.zh: 延伯遂大敗，死傷近二萬人，寶寅收眾退保安定。

translations.literal: Yanbo then suffered a great defeat, with nearly twenty thousand dead and wounded; Baoyin gathered the troops and withdrew to secure Anding.
translations.idiomatic: Yanbo was routed, with nearly twenty thousand dead and wounded; Baoyin pulled back to Anding.

sentences.zh: 延伯自恥其敗，乃繕甲兵，募驍勇，復自安定西進，去賊七里結營。

translations.literal: Yanbo, ashamed of his defeat, then repaired armor and weapons, recruited fierce warriors, and again advanced west from Anding, encamping seven li from the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Humiliated, Yanbo rearmed, recruited bold fighters, and advanced again from Anding, camp seven li from the enemy.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，不告寶寅，獨出襲賊，大破之，俄頃，平其數柵。

translations.literal: On renchen, without informing Baoyin, he went out alone to surprise the rebels and inflicted a great defeat; in a moment he leveled several of their stockades.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen, without telling Baoyin, he raided alone and smashed the rebels, leveling several palisades in minutes.

sentences.zh: 賊見軍士采掠散亂，復還擊之，魏兵大敗，延伯中流矢卒，士卒死者萬餘人。

translations.literal: The rebels saw the soldiers scattered in plunder and struck again; the Wei army suffered a great defeat, Yanbo was struck by a flying arrow and died, and more than ten thousand soldiers were killed.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the troops looting in disorder, the rebels counterattacked; the Wei army collapsed, Yanbo took an arrow and died, and more than ten thousand soldiers fell.

sentences.zh: 時大寇未平，復失驍將，朝野為之憂恐。

translations.literal: At a time when great marauders were not yet pacified and a fierce general was again lost, court and commoners were anxious and afraid for this.
translations.idiomatic: With the great rebellion still raging and a champion general lost, court and country trembled.

sentences.zh: 於是賊勢愈盛，而群臣自外來者，太后問之，皆言賊弱，以求悅媚，由是將帥求益兵者往往不與。

translations.literal: Thereupon the rebels' momentum grew ever stronger, while ministers coming from outside all told the Empress Dowager the rebels were weak, seeking to please and flatter; for this reason commanders who asked for more troops were often refused.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels grew bolder, while ministers arriving from the provinces told the empress dowager the enemy was weak, flattering her; generals who begged for reinforcements were often denied.

sentences.zh: 五月，夷陵烈侯裴邃卒。

translations.literal: Fifth month: Marquis of Yiling Pei Sui died.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, Pei Sui, Marquis of Yiling, died.

sentences.zh: 邃沉深有思略，為政寬明，將吏愛而憚之。

translations.literal: Sui was deep and reserved, with thought and strategy; in governing he was lenient and clear, and officers and clerks both loved and feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Sui was thoughtful and far-sighted, lenient yet clear in command; his officers loved and feared him.

sentences.zh: 壬子，以中護軍夏侯但督壽陽諸軍事，馳驛代邃。

translations.literal: On renzi, Central Guards Commander Xiahou Dan was made Commander of military affairs at Shouyang and rushed by post to replace Sui.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi, Xiahou Dan, central guards commander, was ordered to Shouyang by urgent dispatch to replace Pei Sui.

sentences.zh: 益州刺史臨汝侯淵猷遣其將樊文熾、蕭世澄等，將兵圍魏益州長史和安於小劍，魏益州刺史邴虯遣統軍河南胡小虎、崔珍寶將兵救之。

translations.literal: Governor of Yizhou Marquis of Linru Yuan You sent his generals Fan Wenchì, Xiao Shicheng, and others to lead troops and besiege Wei's Chief Clerk of Yizhou He An at Xiaojian; Wei's Governor of Yizhou Bing Chou sent Commanders Hu Xiaohu of Henan and Cui Zhenbao with troops to rescue him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan You, governor of Yizhou and marquis of Linru, sent Fan Wenchì, Xiao Shicheng, and others to besiege He's chief clerk He An at Xiaojian; Wei's governor Bing Chou sent commanders Hu Xiaohu of Henan and Cui Zhenbao to relieve him.

sentences.zh: 文熾襲破其柵，皆擒之，使小虎於城下說和安令早降。

translations.literal: Wenchì surprised and broke their stockade, capturing them all, and had Xiaohu below the city persuade He An to surrender early.
translations.idiomatic: Wenchì stormed their camp, took all prisoners, and set Xiaohu under the walls to urge He An to yield.

sentences.zh: 小虎遙謂安曰：「我柵失備，為賊所擒，觀其兵力，殊不足言。

translations.literal: Xiaohu called from afar to An, "My stockade lacked defense and I was captured by the enemy; judging their strength, they are hardly worth mention.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaohu shouted up to An, "Our camp was surprised and I was taken; their numbers are nothing.

sentences.zh: 努力堅守，魏行台、傅梁州援兵已至。

translations.literal: " Strive to hold firm—the Wei commissioner and Governor Fu Liangzhou's relief troops have already arrived."
translations.idiomatic: " Hold fast—the Wei commissioner and Governor Fu's relief is here."

sentences.zh: 」語未終，軍士以刀毆殺之。

translations.literal: Before he finished speaking, soldiers hacked him to death with blades.
translations.idiomatic: Before he finished, soldiers cut him down.

sentences.zh: 西南道軍司淳於誕引兵救小劍，文熾置柵於龍鬚山上以防歸路。

translations.literal: Army Supervisor of the Southwestern Route Chunyu Dan led troops to rescue Xiaojian. Wenchì set stockades on Longxu Mountain to block the return road.
translations.idiomatic: Chunyu Dan, army supervisor on the southwestern route, marched to relieve Xiaojian; Wenchì fortified Longxu Mountain to cut the retreat.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，誕密募壯士夜登山燒其柵，梁軍望見歸路絕，皆恟懼。

translations.literal: On wuchen, Dan secretly recruited stalwart men to climb the mountain by night and burn the stockades; the Liang army saw the return road cut and all were fearful.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen, Dan sent bold men by night to burn the palisades on the mountain; the Liang troops, seeing escape blocked, panicked.

sentences.zh: 誕乘而擊之，文熾大敗，僅以身免。

translations.literal: Dan seized the moment and struck; Wenchì suffered a great defeat and barely escaped with his life.
translations.idiomatic: Dan struck at once; Wenchì was routed and fled alone.

sentences.zh: 虜世澄等將吏十一人，斬獲萬計。

translations.literal: They captured Shicheng and eleven other officers and clerks, beheading and capturing tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: They seized Shicheng and ten other officers, with tens of thousands killed or captured.

sentences.zh: 魏子建以世澄購胡小虎之屍，得而葬之。

translations.literal: Wei Zijian used Shicheng to purchase the corpse of Hu Xiaohu, obtained it, and buried it.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zijian ransomed Hu Xiaohu's body through Shicheng and gave him burial.

sentences.zh: 魏魏昌武康伯李崇卒。

translations.literal: Wei Marquis of Weichang Wukang Bo Li Chong died.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chong, marquis of Weichang and Baron Wukang, died.

sentences.zh: 初，帝納齊東昏侯寵姬吳淑媛，七月而生豫章王綜，宮中多疑之。

translations.literal: Initially, the Emperor took as consort Wu Shuyuan, a favored concubine of the Marquis of Qi, the Eastern Deposed Emperor; in the seventh month she bore Prince of Yuzhang Zong, and within the palace many doubted this.
translations.idiomatic: Long ago the emperor had taken Wu Shuyuan, a favorite of Qi’s deposed emperor Dong Hunhou; she bore Prince Zong of Yuzhang in the seventh month, and the palace murmured.

sentences.zh: 及淑媛寵衰怨望，密謂綜曰：「汝七月生兒，安得比諸皇子！

translations.literal: When Shuyuan's favor waned she resented and looked askance; secretly she told Zong, "You were born in the seventh month—how can you compare with the other princes!
translations.idiomatic: When Shuyuan's favor faded she grew bitter and whispered to Zong, "A seventh-month child—how can you rank with the other princes?

sentences.zh: 然汝太子次弟，幸保富貴，勿洩也！

translations.literal: " Yet you are next after the crown prince in seniority; fortunately preserve wealth and honor—do not reveal this!"
translations.idiomatic: " Yet you stand next to the heir; guard your fortune and tell no one!"

sentences.zh: 」與綜相抱而泣。

translations.literal: She and Zong embraced and wept.
translations.idiomatic: Mother and son wept in each other's arms.

sentences.zh: 綜由是自疑，晝則談虐如常，夜則於靜室閉戶，披髮席稿，私於別室祭齊氏七廟。

translations.literal: Zong thereby came to doubt himself; by day he spoke and acted cruelly as usual, but by night in a quiet chamber he shut the door, let down his hair, and spread straw for a mat, privately in a separate room sacrificing to the seven temples of the Qi house.
translations.idiomatic: From then Zong lived in secret doubt: by day he played the brutal prince, by night behind closed doors, hair loose on straw mats, he worshipped the seven temples of Qi in a hidden room.

sentences.zh: 又微服至曲阿拜齊太宗陵，聞俗說割血瀝骨，滲則為父子，遂潛發東昏侯塚，並自殺一男試之，皆驗。

translations.literal: He also went in plain dress to Qu'e to bow at the tomb of Emperor Taizong of Qi; hearing the folk tale that if blood dripped on bone and seeped in they were father and son, he secretly opened the tomb of the Eastern Deposed Emperor and also killed a boy of his own to test it—both proved true.
translations.idiomatic: He visited Qu'e in disguise to bow at Qi Taizong's tomb; hearing that blood dripped on bone that absorbs it proves kinship, he opened Dong Hunhou's grave and killed one of his own sons to test it—both times the blood sank in.

sentences.zh: 由是常懷異志，專伺時變。

translations.literal: Thereby he constantly harbored a different intent and watched solely for a change in the times.
translations.idiomatic: He nursed treason ever after and watched for his moment.

sentences.zh: 綜有勇力，能手制奔馬；

translations.literal: Zong had courage and strength and could with his hands subdue a galloping horse;
translations.idiomatic: Zong was strong enough to halt a runaway horse with his bare hands;

sentences.zh: 輕財好士，唯留附身故衣，餘皆分施，恆致罄乏。

translations.literal: he was light with wealth and fond of knights; he kept only the clothes of his personal attendants and gave away the rest, constantly ending in want.
translations.idiomatic: he spent freely and gathered adventurers, keeping only his servants' old clothes and giving away the rest until he was often broke.

sentences.zh: 屢上便宜，求為邊任，上未之許。

translations.literal: Repeatedly he submitted practical proposals asking for frontier duty; the Emperor did not grant it.
translations.idiomatic: Again and again he asked for a border command; the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 常於內齋布沙於地，終日跣行，足下生胝，日能行三百里。

translations.literal: He constantly spread sand on the floor of his inner study and walked barefoot all day until calluses formed on his soles; he could walk three hundred li in a day.
translations.idiomatic: He spread sand in his private study and walked barefoot until his feet blistered, training to march three hundred li in a day.

sentences.zh: 王、侯、妃、主及外人皆知其志，而上性嚴重，人莫敢言。

translations.literal: Kings, marquises, consorts, princesses, and outsiders all knew his intent, but the Emperor's nature was stern and weighty and none dared speak.
translations.idiomatic: Princes, consorts, and courtiers knew his mind, but the emperor's severity silenced them.

sentences.zh: 又使通問於蕭寶寅，謂之叔父。

translations.literal: He also sent secret messages to Xiao Baoyin, calling him uncle.
translations.idiomatic: He also corresponded secretly with Xiao Baoyin, calling him uncle.

sentences.zh: 為南兗州刺史，不見賓客，辭訟隔簾聽之，出則垂帷於輿，惡人識其面。

translations.literal: As Governor of Southern Yanzhou he did not receive guests; he heard lawsuits through a screen, and when going out hung curtains on his carriage, hating that people recognize his face.
translations.idiomatic: As governor of southern Yanzhou he refused visitors, judged cases behind a screen, and veiled his carriage when he went abroad.

sentences.zh: 及在彭城，魏安豐王延明、臨淮王彧將兵二萬逼彭城，勝負久未決。

translations.literal: When at Pengcheng, Wei's Prince of Anfeng Yanming and Prince of Linhuai Yu led twenty thousand troops to press Pengcheng; victory and defeat long remained undecided.
translations.idiomatic: At Pengcheng, Yuan Yanming of Anfeng and Yuan Yu of Linhuai pressed the city with twenty thousand men; the outcome hung long in the balance.

sentences.zh: 上慮綜敗沒，敕綜引軍還。

translations.literal: The Emperor feared Zong would be defeated and lost; he ordered Zong to withdraw the army.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing Zong would be lost, the emperor ordered him to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 綜恐南歸不復得至北邊，乃密遣人送降款於彧；

translations.literal: Zong feared that if he returned south he would never reach the northern border again; he secretly sent a man to deliver terms of surrender to Yu;
translations.idiomatic: Zong feared that going south meant never returning north; he secretly sent surrender terms to Yuan Yu;

sentences.zh: 魏人皆不之信，彧募人入綜軍驗其虛實，無敢行者。

translations.literal: the Wei people all did not believe it. Yu recruited someone to enter Zong's army to verify the truth or falsehood, and none dared go.
translations.idiomatic: the Wei side did not believe him. Yu sought a volunteer to enter Zong's camp to test the offer, and no one would go.

sentences.zh: 殿中侍御史濟陰鹿悆為彧監軍，請行，曰：「若綜有誠心，與之盟約；

translations.literal: Palace Attendant of the Hall Lu Yu of Jiyin, as Yu's supervising army officer, asked to go and said, "If Zong is sincere, make a covenant with him;
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yu of Jiyin, palace attendant of the hall and Yu's army supervisor, volunteered: "If Zong is sincere, we swear an oath;

sentences.zh: 如其詐也，何惜一夫！

translations.literal: " if it is deception, what is one man worth!
translations.idiomatic: " if he lies, what is one man's life?"

sentences.zh: 」時兩敵相對，內外嚴固，單騎間出，逕趣彭城，為綜軍所執，問其來狀，彧曰：「臨淮王使我來，欲有交易耳。

translations.literal: " At that time the two armies faced each other, inner and outer defenses strict; riding out alone between the lines, he went straight to Pengcheng and was seized by Zong's troops. Asked his purpose, Yu said, "The Prince of Linhuai sent me—there is a deal to discuss."
translations.idiomatic: " The armies stood face to face, guards tight on every side. Lu Yu rode out alone straight to Pengcheng, where Zong's men seized him. When they asked why he had come, he said, "Prince Linhuai sent me to negotiate."

sentences.zh: 」時元略已南還，綜聞之，謂成景俊等曰：「我常疑元略規欲反城，將驗其虛實，故遣左右為略使，入魏軍中，呼彼一人。

translations.literal: " At that time Yuan Lue had already returned south. Hearing this, Zong said to Cheng Jingjun and others, "I always suspected Yuan Lue meant to turn the city over; to test whether this is real, I sent attendants posing as Lue's envoys into the Wei camp to summon one of their men."
translations.idiomatic: " Yuan Lue had already gone south. When Zong heard of Lu Yu's arrival, he told Cheng Jingjun and the others, "I have long suspected Lue meant to hand over the city. I sent men disguised as his envoys into the Wei lines to call one of them forward and see what would happen."

sentences.zh: 令其人果來，可遣人詐為略有疾在深室，呼至戶外，令人傳言謝之。

translations.literal: If that man truly comes, we can send someone feigning that Lue is ill in an inner chamber, call him to the doorway, and have a man convey apologies.
translations.idiomatic: If he comes, we will pretend Lue is ill in an inner room, summon the man to the threshold, and send out word of apology.

sentences.zh: 」綜又遣腹心安定梁話迎悆，密以意狀語之。

translations.literal: " Zong also sent his trusted retainer An Ding Liang Hua to meet Yu and secretly told him the plan.
translations.idiomatic: " Zong also sent his confidant Liang Hua of Anding to receive Lu Yu and quietly explain the plan.

sentences.zh: 悆薄暮入城，先引見胡龍牙，龍牙曰：「元中山甚欲相見，故遣呼卿。

translations.literal: Yu entered the city at dusk and was first led to Hu Longya. Longya said, "Yuan Zhongshan very much wishes to see you and therefore sent to summon you."
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yu entered the city at dusk and was brought first to Hu Longya, who said, "Yuan Zhongshan is eager to see you—that is why he sent for you."

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「安豐、臨淮，將少弱卒，規復此城，容可得乎！

translations.literal: He also said, "Anfeng and Linhuai lead weak young troops planning to recover this city—can they possibly succeed!"
translations.idiomatic: He added, "Anfeng and Linhuai are here with a thin force of green boys, hoping to retake this city—do they really think they can?"

sentences.zh: 」悆曰：「彭城，魏之東鄙，勢在必爭，得否在天，非人所測。

translations.literal: " Yu said, "Pengcheng is Wei's eastern frontier; both sides are bound to fight for it. Success or failure lies with Heaven, not something men can foretell."
translations.idiomatic: " Lu Yu answered, "Pengcheng is the eastern gate of Wei—both sides must fight for it. Whether it falls is heaven's doing, not ours to guess."

sentences.zh: 」龍牙曰：「當如卿言。

translations.literal: " Longya said, "It should be as you say."
translations.idiomatic: " Longya said, "No doubt you are right."

sentences.zh: 」又引見成景俊，景俊與坐，謂曰：「卿不為刺客邪！

translations.literal: He was also led to Cheng Jingjun. Jingjun sat with him and said, "You are not an assassin, are you!"
translations.idiomatic: He was then taken to Cheng Jingjun, who sat with him and asked, "You are not here as an assassin, are you?"

sentences.zh: 」悆曰：「今者奉使，欲返命本朝。

translations.literal: " Yu said, "Today I come on mission and wish to return and report to my court. As for stabbing—let us choose another occasion."
translations.idiomatic: " Lu Yu said, "I am on embassy today and must report back to my court. If there is to be killing, let it wait for another day."

sentences.zh: 相刺之事，更卜後圖。

translations.literal: As for assassination, we shall choose another occasion.
translations.idiomatic: As for killing, let that wait for another day.

sentences.zh: 」景俊為設飲食，乃引至一所，詐令一人自室中出，為元略致意曰：「我昔有以南向，且遣相呼，欲聞鄉事；

translations.literal: As for assassination, we shall choose another occasion.
translations.idiomatic: As for killing, let that wait for another day.

sentences.zh: 晚來疾作，不獲相見。

translations.literal: " Yu said, "Long ago I received your word and ventured here despite danger; failing to glimpse you, my heart is unsettled."
translations.idiomatic: " Lu Yu said, "I came at your word through great risk and could not see you—my heart is uneasy."

sentences.zh: 」悆曰：「早奉音旨，冒險祗赴，不得瞻見，內懷反側。

translations.literal: Then he withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Then he took his leave.

sentences.zh: 」遂辭退。

translations.literal: Illness came on in the evening and I could not meet you.
translations.idiomatic: Sickness came at evening and I could not receive you.

sentences.zh: 諸將競問魏士馬多少，悆盛陳有勁兵數十萬。

translations.literal: The generals competed in asking how many Wei soldiers and horses there were; Yu extravagantly declared there were several hundred thousand stalwart troops.
translations.idiomatic: The generals crowded around asking how large the Wei host was; Lu Yu declared hundreds of thousands of crack troops.

sentences.zh: 諸將相謂曰：「此華辭耳！

translations.literal: The generals said to one another, "These are boastful words!"
translations.idiomatic: The generals muttered, "Empty boasting!"

sentences.zh: 」悆曰：「崇朝可驗，何華之有！

translations.literal: " Yu said, "By tomorrow morning it can be verified—what boasting is there!"
translations.idiomatic: " Lu Yu said, "Wait until morning and you will see—where is the boast?"

sentences.zh: 」乃遣悆還。

translations.literal: " Then they sent Yu back.
translations.idiomatic: " They sent Lu Yu back.

sentences.zh: 景俊送之於戲馬台，北望城塹，謂曰：「險固如此，豈魏所能取！

translations.literal: Jingjun escorted him to Terrace of Sporting Horses, looked north at the moat and ramparts, and said, "So fortified—how could Wei take it!"
translations.idiomatic: Jingjun walked him to the Terrace of Sporting Horses, gazed north at walls and moat, and said, "Defenses like these—how could Wei ever take the city?"

sentences.zh: 」悆曰：「攻守在人，何論險固！

translations.literal: " Yu said, "Attack and defense depend on men—what talk of fortifications!"
translations.idiomatic: " Lu Yu replied, "Walls win or lose through men—not through stone."

sentences.zh: 」悆還，於路復與梁話申固盟約。

translations.literal: " Yu on the return road again with Liang Hua renewed their secret covenant.
translations.idiomatic: " On the road home Lu Yu and Liang Hua renewed their secret pact.

sentences.zh: 六月，庚辰，綜與梁話及淮陰苗文寵夜出，步投彧軍。

translations.literal: Sixth month, gengchen: Zong with Liang Hua and Huaiyin Miao Wenchong slipped out by night on foot and went to Yu's army.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on gengchen, Zong slipped out on foot by night with Liang Hua and Miao Wenchong of Huaiyin and made for Yuan Yu's camp.

sentences.zh: 及旦，齋內諸閣猶閉不開，眾莫知所以，唯見城外魏軍呼曰：「汝豫章王昨夜已來，在我軍中，汝尚何為！

translations.literal: When dawn came the various gates of the fast still stood closed; none knew why, only seeing outside the Wei army shout, "Your Prince of Yuzhang came last night to our army—what are you still doing!"
translations.idiomatic: At dawn the inner gates were still shut and no one knew why, until the Wei soldiers outside shouted, "Your Prince of Yuzhang is already with us—what are you waiting for?"

sentences.zh: 」城中求王不獲，軍遂大潰。

translations.literal: The city sought the prince but could not find him; the army thereupon collapsed utterly.
translations.idiomatic: The city searched for the prince in vain, and the army collapsed.

sentences.zh: 魏人入彭城，乘勝追擊梁兵，復取諸城，至宿豫而還。

translations.literal: Wei men entered Pengcheng, pursued the Liang army with victory, recovered the various cities, and returned as far as Suyu.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei troops entered Pengcheng, chased the Liang forces, retook the lost towns, and withdrew as far as Suyu.

sentences.zh: 將佐士卒死沒者什七八，唯陳慶之帥所部得還。

translations.literal: Officers, assistants, soldiers—seven or eight in ten died or were lost; only Chen Qingzhi led his division back intact.
translations.idiomatic: Seven or eight tenths of the officers and men were killed or lost; only Chen Qingzhi brought his command out whole.

sentences.zh: 上聞之，驚駭，有司奏削綜爵士，絕屬籍，更其子直姓悖氏。

translations.literal: The Emperor heard it, was shocked, and the relevant office memorialized to strip Zong of his marquisate and cut him from the clan registers, changing his son Zhi's surname to Bo.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was appalled. The ministry memorialized to strip Zong of rank and expel him from the clan rolls, changing his son Zhi's surname to Bo.

sentences.zh: 未旬日，詔復屬籍，封直為永新侯。

translations.literal: Within ten days an edict restored him to the registers and enfeoffed Zhi as Marquis of Yongxin.
translations.idiomatic: Within ten days an edict restored the clan registers and made Zhi marquis of Yongxin.

sentences.zh: 西豐侯正德自魏還，志行無悛，多聚亡命，夜剽掠殺人於道，以輕車將軍從綜北伐，棄軍輒還。

translations.literal: Marquis of Xifeng Zhengde returned from Wei; his conduct was unrepentant. He gathered many fugitives and by night robbed and killed on the roads. As General of Agile Cavalry he followed Zong on the northern campaign, abandoned the army and returned without leave.
translations.idiomatic: Marquis Zhengde of Xifeng had returned from Wei unchanged, gathering fugitives and murdering travelers by night. He had followed Zong north as general of agile cavalry, then deserted and came home without leave.

sentences.zh: 上積其前後罪惡，免官削爵，徙臨海；

translations.literal: The Emperor accumulated his past and present crimes, removed him from office and stripped his rank, and exiled him to Linhai;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor tallied his crimes old and new, stripped his office and titles, and banished him toward Linhai;

sentences.zh: 未至，追赦之。

translations.literal: before he arrived, a pursuative pardon was granted.
translations.idiomatic: before he arrived a pardon overtook him.

sentences.zh: 綜至洛陽，見魏主，還就館，為齊東昏侯舉哀，服斬衰三年。

translations.literal: Zong reached Luoyang and saw the Wei sovereign; returning to his quarters, he performed mourning for the Eastern Deposed Emperor of Qi, wearing the hemp of the keenest grief for three years.
translations.idiomatic: Zong reached Luoyang, was received by the Wei emperor, and in his quarters mourned Qi's deposed emperor Dong Hunhou in the deepest hemp for three years.

sentences.zh: 太后以下並就館吊之，賞賜禮遇甚厚，拜司空，封高平郡公、丹陽王，更名贊。

translations.literal: From the Empress Dowager down all came to the quarters to condole; rewards and courtesy were very generous. He was appointed Minister of Works, enfeoffed as Duke of Gaoping commandery and Prince of Danyang, and his name was changed to Zan.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager and the court called to condole; honors flowed. He was made minister of works, duke of Gaoping and prince of Danyang, and renamed Zan.

sentences.zh: 以苗文寵、梁話皆為光祿大夫；

translations.literal: Miao Wenchong and Liang Hua were both made Masters of Splendor;
translations.idiomatic: Miao Wenchong and Liang Hua were both named masters of splendor;

sentences.zh: 封鹿悆為定陶縣子，除員外散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Lu Yu was enfeoffed as Viscount of Dingtao county and appointed Supernumerary Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yu was created viscount of Dingtao and made supernumerary regular attendant.

sentences.zh: 綜長史濟陽江革、司馬范陽祖□恆之皆為魏所虜，安豐王延明聞其才名，厚遇之。

translations.literal: Zong's chief clerk Jiang Ge of Jiyang and marshal Zu □ Hengzhi of Fanyang were all captured by Wei. Prince of Anfeng Yanming heard their literary renown and treated them generously.
translations.idiomatic: Zong's chief clerk Jiang Ge of Jiyang and marshal Zu □ Hengzhi of Fanyang were taken by Wei. Yuan Yanming of Anfeng, hearing of their talent, treated them well.

sentences.zh: 革稱足疾不拜。

translations.literal: Ge claimed foot ailment and would not bow.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Ge pleaded foot trouble and refused to bow.

sentences.zh: 延明使□恆之作《欹器漏刻銘》，革唾罵□恆之曰：「卿荷國厚恩，乃為虜立銘，孤負朝廷！

translations.literal: Yanming had □ Hengzhi compose the "Inscription for the Tilting Vessel and Clepsydra." Ge spat and reviled □ Hengzhi, "You bear the state's deep grace yet compose an inscription for the captors—you betray the court!"
translations.idiomatic: Yanming set □ Hengzhi to write an inscription for the tilting vessel and water clock. Jiang Ge cursed him: "The state favored you, and you write for the enemy—you betray the court!"

sentences.zh: 」延明聞之，令革作《大小寺碑》、《祭彭祖文》，革辭不為。

translations.literal: " Hearing this, Yanming ordered Ge to compose the "Stele of Great and Small Temples" and "Text for Sacrifice to Peng Zu"; Ge refused.
translations.idiomatic: " Yanming then ordered Jiang Ge to write steles for the great and small temples and a sacrifice to Peng Zu; Jiang Ge refused.

sentences.zh: 延明將棰之，革厲色曰：「江革行年六十，今日得死為幸，誓不為人執筆！

translations.literal: Yanming was about to beat him. Ge said with stern countenance, "Jiang Ge has lived sixty years; to die today would be fortune—I swear not to hold the brush for others!"
translations.idiomatic: Yanming raised a staff to beat him. Jiang Ge said coldly, "I am sixty; to die now would be a mercy—I will never write at your command!"

sentences.zh: 」延明知不可屈，乃止；

translations.literal: " Yanming knew he could not be bent and desisted;
translations.idiomatic: " Yanming saw he would not bend and stopped;

sentences.zh: 日給脫粟三升，僅全其生而已。

translations.literal: each day they gave three sheng of husked millet—barely enough to preserve life.
translations.idiomatic: each day they gave him three pints of husked millet—barely enough to live.

sentences.zh: 上密召夏侯但還，使休兵合肥，俟淮堰成復進。

translations.literal: The Emperor secretly recalled Xiahou Dan, had him rest the army at Hefei, and wait until the Huai dyke was complete before advancing again.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor secretly recalled Xiahou Dan, rested the army at Hefei, and waited for the Huai dyke to be finished before advancing again.

sentences.zh: 癸未，魏大赦，改元孝昌。

translations.literal: On guiwei Wei proclaimed a general amnesty and changed the era name to Xiaochang.
translations.idiomatic: On guiwei Wei declared a general amnesty and proclaimed the era Xiaochang.

sentences.zh: 破六韓拔陵圍魏廣陽王深於五原，軍主賀拔勝募二百人開東門出戰，斬首百餘級，賊稍退。

translations.literal: Poliuhan Baling besieged Wei's Prince of Guangyang Shen at Wuyuan. Garrison Commander Heba Sheng recruited two hundred men, opened the east gate and went out to fight, cut off more than a hundred heads, and the rebels drew back slightly.
translations.idiomatic: Poliuhan Baling besieged Yuan Shen, prince of Guangyang, at Wuyuan. Garrison commander Heba Sheng took two hundred men out the east gate, struck, and took more than a hundred heads; the rebels slackened.

sentences.zh: 深拔軍向明州，勝常為殿。

translations.literal: Shen withdrew the army toward Mingzhou; Sheng often served as rearguard.
translations.idiomatic: Shen drew off toward Mingzhou, with Sheng often covering the rear.

sentences.zh: 雲州刺史費穆，招撫離散，四面拒敵。

translations.literal: Governor of Yunzhou Fei Mu recruited and soothed the scattered, resisting on all sides.
translations.idiomatic: Fei Mu, governor of Yunzhou, gathered the scattered and fought on every side.

sentences.zh: 時北境州鎮皆沒，唯雲中一城獨存。

translations.literal: At the time northern border provinces and garrisons all fell; only Yunyang city alone remained.
translations.idiomatic: Every northern garrison had fallen; only the city of Yunzhong still held.

sentences.zh: 久之，道路阻絕，援軍不至，糧仗俱盡，穆棄城南奔爾朱榮於秀容；

translations.literal: After long time roads were cut and relief did not come; provisions and weapons were exhausted. Mu abandoned the city and fled south to Erzhu Rong at Xiurong;
translations.idiomatic: When roads were cut and no relief came, with food and arms gone, Mu abandoned the city and fled south to Erzhu Rong at Xiurong;

sentences.zh: 既而詣闕請罪，詔原之。

translations.literal: afterward he came to court to beg punishment; an edict pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: then he presented himself at court to accept punishment and was pardoned.

sentences.zh: 長流參軍於謹言於廣陽王深曰：「今寇盜蜂起，未易專用武力勝也。

translations.literal: Chief clerk Yu Jin said to Prince of Guangyang Shen, "Now bandits and robbers rise like bees—it is not easy to overcome them by martial force alone. Jin asks to bear the great prince's authority and persuade them with fortune and disaster—perhaps many can gradually be detached."
translations.idiomatic: Staff officer Yu Jin told Prince Guangyang Shen, "Bandits swarm everywhere—force alone will not end this. Let me ride out under your authority and offer mercy or ruin; many may peel away."

sentences.zh: 謹請奉大王之威命，諭以禍福，庶幾稍可離也。

translations.literal: Jin asks to bear the great prince's authority and persuade them with fortune and disaster—perhaps many can gradually be detached."
translations.idiomatic: Let me ride out under your authority and offer mercy or ruin; many may peel away."

sentences.zh: 」深許之。

translations.literal: " Shen consented.
translations.idiomatic: " Shen agreed.

sentences.zh: 謹兼通諸國語，乃單騎詣叛胡營，見其酋長，開示恩信，於是西部鐵勒酋長乜列河等將三萬餘戶南詣深降。

translations.literal: Shen wished to lead troops to Zhefu Ridge to welcome them. Jin said, "Poliuhan Baling's military momentum is very strong; hearing Yiliehe and others come to surrender, he is sure to lead troops to intercept. If he first seizes difficult passes, he is not easy to match. Better use Yiliehe as bait and set ambush troops to await him—he can surely be broken."
translations.idiomatic: Shen wanted to march to Zhefu Ridge to welcome them. Jin said, "Baling is strong; hearing of the surrender he will intercept. Seize the passes first and he is hard to beat. Better bait him with Yiliehe and ambush—then he can be broken."

sentences.zh: 深欲引兵至折敷嶺迎之，謹曰：「破六韓拔陵兵勢甚盛，聞乜列河等來降，必引兵邀之，若先據險要，未易敵也。

translations.literal: Shen followed this. Baling indeed led troops to intercept and strike Yiliehe and captured all his multitude;
translations.idiomatic: Shen agreed. Baling did intercept Yiliehe and took all his people;

sentences.zh: 不若以乜列河餌之，而伏兵以待之，必可破也。

translations.literal: Better not use Yiliehe as bait and set ambush troops to await him—he can surely be broken.
translations.idiomatic: Better offer Yiliehe as bait, hide troops, and strike—then he can be shattered.

sentences.zh: 」深從之，拔陵果引兵邀擊乜列河，盡俘其眾；

translations.literal: " Shen followed this. Baling indeed led troops to intercept and strike Yiliehe and captured all his multitude;
translations.idiomatic: " Shen agreed. Baling did intercept Yiliehe and took all his people;

sentences.zh: 伏兵發，拔陵大敗，復得乜列河之眾而還。

translations.literal: Rouran Chileantou Khan inflicted a great defeat on Poliuhan Baling and beheaded his generals Kongque and others.
translations.idiomatic: The Rouran khan Chileantou crushed Poliuhan Baling and beheaded generals such as Kongque.

sentences.zh: 柔然頭兵可汗大破破六韓拔陵，斬其將孔雀等。

translations.literal: Baling avoided the Rouran, moved south and crossed the river.
translations.idiomatic: Baling fled the Rouran, moved south, and crossed the river.

sentences.zh: 拔陵避柔然，南徙渡河。

translations.literal: General Li Shuren because Baling pressed closer sought aid from Prince of Guangyang Shen; Shen led troops to go to him.
translations.idiomatic: General Li Shuren, pressed by Baling, begged aid from Prince Guangyang; Shen marched to his relief.

sentences.zh: 將軍李叔仁以拔陵稍逼，求援於廣陽王深，深帥眾赴之。

translations.literal: Rebels who surrendered before and after numbered two hundred thousand. Shen and Commissioner Yuan Zuan memorialized, "We beg to establish separately counties north of Hengzhou to settle surrendered households, grant relief as appropriate, and quiet their rebellious hearts."
translations.idiomatic: Two hundred thousand rebels had surrendered. Shen and commissioner Yuan Zuan memorialized to set up new counties north of Hengzhou to settle them and quiet their hearts.

sentences.zh: 賊前後降附者二十萬人，深與行台元纂表：「乞於恆州北別立郡縣，安置降戶，隨宜賑賚，息其亂心。

translations.literal: The Wei court did not consent and ordered Yellow Gate Attendant Yang Yu to distribute them among Ji, Ding, and Ying provinces to find food.
translations.idiomatic: The court refused and ordered Yang Yu to scatter them through Ji, Ding, and Ying to find food.

sentences.zh: 」魏朝不從，詔黃門侍郎楊昱分處之於冀、定、瀛三州就食。

translations.literal: Shen said to Zuan, "These people will beg to live again."
translations.idiomatic: Shen told Zuan, "They will have to beg for their lives again."

sentences.zh: 深謂纂曰：「此輩復為乞活矣。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, renxu: general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on renxu, there was a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，壬戌，大赦。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, renxu: general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on renxu, there was a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 八月，魏柔玄鎮民杜洛周聚眾反於上谷，改元真王，攻沒郡縣，高歡、蔡俊、尉景及段榮、安定彭樂皆從之。

translations.literal: Jing was Shuang's grandson.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Jing was a grandson of Chang Shuang.

sentences.zh: 洛周圍魏燕州刺史博陵崔秉，九月，丙辰，魏以幽州刺史常景兼尚書為行台，與幽州都督元譚討之。

translations.literal: From Lulong Pass to Jundu Pass troops were all posted to guard the perilous routes; Tan encamped at Juyong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: From Lulong Pass to Jundu Pass troops guarded every defile; Yuan Tan held Juyong Pass.

sentences.zh: 景，爽之孫也。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month: Tuyuhun sent troops to attack Zhao Tian'an; Tian'an surrendered and Liangzhou again belonged to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, Tuyuhun attacked Zhao Tian'an; he surrendered and Liangzhou returned to Wei.

sentences.zh: 自盧龍塞至軍都關，皆置兵守險，譚屯居庸關。

translations.literal: From Lulong Pass to Jundu Pass troops were all posted to guard the perilous routes; Tan encamped at Juyong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: From Lulong Pass to Jundu Pass troops guarded every defile; Yuan Tan held Juyong Pass.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，吐谷渾遣兵擊趙天安，天安降，涼州復為魏。

translations.literal: General Who Pacifies the West Gao Hui went on mission to the Ephthalites; returning, he reached Fuhan.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Hui, general who pacifies the west, returning from embassy to the Ephthalites, reached Fuhan.

sentences.zh: 平西將軍高徽奉使厭噠，還，至枹罕。

translations.literal: It happened that Governor of Hezhou Yuan Zuo died. Former governor Liang Zhao's son Jingjin led Moqi Niansheng's troops to besiege the city.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Yuan Zuo of Hezhou died. Liang Jingjin, son of the former governor Liang Zhao, brought Moqi Niansheng's troops to besiege the city.

sentences.zh: 會河州刺史元祚卒，前刺史梁釗之子景進引莫折念生兵圍其城。

translations.literal: Chief clerk Yuan Yong and others pushed Hui to act as governor pro tem and urged troops to hold firm;
translations.idiomatic: Chief clerk Yuan Yong and others made Gao Hui acting governor and held the walls;

sentences.zh: 長史元永等推徽行州事，勒兵固守；

translations.literal: Jingjin also himself acted as governor.
translations.idiomatic: Jingjin claimed the governorship as well.

sentences.zh: 景進亦自行州事。

translations.literal: Hui requested troops from Tuyuhun; Tuyuhun rescued them and Jingjin was defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Hui called on Tuyuhun; they came, Jingjin was beaten, and fled.

sentences.zh: 徽請兵於吐谷渾，吐谷渾救之，景進敗走。

translations.literal: Hui was Hu's grandson.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Hui was a grandson of Gao Hu.

sentences.zh: 徽，湖之孫也。

translations.literal: Hui was Hu's grandson.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Hui was a grandson of Gao Hu.

sentences.zh: 魏方有事西北，二荊、西郢群蠻皆反，斷三鴉路，殺都督，寇掠，北至襄城。

translations.literal: On the Ru River were the Ran, Xiang, and Tian clans—their tribes most flourishing; the rest, large ones ten thousand households, small ones a thousand dwellings, each called themselves kings and marquises, encamped in strong passes, roads impassable.
translations.idiomatic: Along the Ru lived the Ran, Xiang, and Tian— the strongest tribes; others, ten thousand households or a thousand, each styled themselves kings and lords, holding the passes so no road was open.

sentences.zh: 汝水有冉氏、向氏、田氏，種落最盛，其餘大者萬家，小者千室，各稱王侯，屯據險要，道路不通。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, renwu: the Wei sovereign issued an edict, "We shall personally lead the Six Armies to sweep away the fugitive filth; now first strike the Jing barbarians and put the southern domain in order."
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on renwu, the Wei emperor proclaimed, "I will lead the six armies to sweep away the rebels; first I strike the Jing barbarians and settle the south."

sentences.zh: 十二月，壬午，魏主下詔曰：「朕將親御六師，掃蕩逋穢，今先討荊蠻，疆理南服。

translations.literal: At the time the various barbarians brought in Liang generals Cao Yizong and others to besiege Wei's Jingzhou. Wei commander Cui Xian led several tens of thousands of men to rescue; reaching Luyang, he dared not advance.
translations.idiomatic: The barbarians called in Liang generals such as Cao Yizong to besiege Jingzhou. Cui Xian marched with tens of thousands to relieve it but halted at Luyang, afraid to go on.

sentences.zh: 」時群蠻引梁將曹義宗等圍魏荊州，魏都督崔暹將兵數萬救之，至魯陽，不敢進。

translations.literal: Wei again made Prince of Linhuai Yu general who campaigns south, leading troops to suppress Luyang barbarians; Director of the Secretariat Chief Clerk Xin Xiong was eastern-route commissioner left aide, marching east toward Yecheng.
translations.idiomatic: Wei again made Yuan Yu of Linhuai general who campaigns south against the Luyang tribes, with Xin Xiong, chief clerk of the Secretariat, as eastern-route aide, marching on Yecheng.

sentences.zh: 魏更以臨淮王彧為征南大將軍，將兵討魯陽蠻，司空長史辛雄為行台左丞，東趣葉城。

translations.literal: Separately they dispatched General Who Subdues the Barbarians Pei Yan and Hengnong Administrator Prince of Jingzhao Pi to lead ten thousand men from Wuguan to open the Sanya road and rescue Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Separately Pei Yan, general who subdues the barbarians, and Yuan Pi of Jingzhao, administrator of Hengnong, were sent with ten thousand men through Wuguan to reopen the Sanya road and save Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 別遣征虜將軍裴衍、恆農太守京兆王羆將兵一萬，自武關出通三鴉路，以救荊州。

translations.literal: Yan and the others had not yet arrived when Yu's army already encamped on the Ru upstream; commanderies and districts harried by barbarians competed to come beg rescue; Yu because places differed on routes did not wish to respond.
translations.idiomatic: Before Pei Yan arrived, Yu was already on the upper Ru; harried districts begged for help, but Yu, citing different routes, would not move.

sentences.zh: 衍等未至，彧軍已屯汝上，州郡被蠻寇者爭來請救，彧以處分道別，不欲應之。
