translations.literal: Xin Xiong said, "Now Pei Yan has not arrived, yet Your Highness's troops and masses are assembled, the barbarians are brash and trouble the near capital. Your Highness holds command beyond the passes—when you see an opening, advance—what talk of separate routes!"
translations.idiomatic: Xin Xiong said, "Pei Yan is not here yet, but your force is ready and the barbarians swagger at the capital's doorstep. You command beyond the passes—strike when you see your chance; why quibble over routes?"

sentences.zh: 辛雄曰：「今裴衍未至，王士眾已集，蠻左唐突，撓亂近畿，王秉麾閫外，見可而進，何論別道！

translations.literal: Yu feared later being held accountable for gain or loss and invited Xiong to issue orders under seal.
translations.idiomatic: Yu feared blame for failure and asked Xin Xiong to issue sealed orders.

sentences.zh: 」彧恐後有得失之責，邀雄符下。

translations.literal: Xiong held that hearing the Wei sovereign would personally go out, their hearts would surely be shaken and they could be broken while momentum served; he then sealed Yu's army ordering swift advance and strike.
translations.idiomatic: Xin Xiong judged that news the emperor would march in person would shake them; he sealed orders for Yu to attack at once.

sentences.zh: 雄以群蠻聞魏主將自出，心必震動，可乘勢破也，遂符彧軍，令速赴擊。

translations.literal: " At that time the various barbarians brought in Liang generals Cao Yizong and others to besiege Wei's Jingzhou. Wei commander Cui Xian led several tens of thousands of men to rescue; reaching Luyang, he dared not advance.
translations.idiomatic: " The tribes called in Liang generals such as Cao Yizong to besiege Jingzhou. Cui Xian marched with tens of thousands to relieve it but halted at Luyang, afraid to advance.

sentences.zh: 群蠻聞之，果散走。

translations.literal: Hearing this, the various barbarians indeed scattered and fled.
translations.idiomatic: When the barbarians heard, they broke and ran.

sentences.zh: 魏主欲自出討賊，中書令袁翻諫而止。

translations.literal: The Wei sovereign wished to go out himself to suppress the bandits; Director of the Secretariat Yuan Fan remonstrated and stopped it.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor meant to take the field himself; Yuan Fan, director of the Secretariat, dissuaded him.

sentences.zh: 辛雄自軍中上疏曰：「凡人所以臨陳忘身，觸白刃而不憚者，一求榮名，二貪重賞，三畏刑罰，四避禍難。

translations.literal: Xin Xiong from the army submitted a memorial, "The reason any man forgets his body before the battle line and does not fear touching white blades is, first to seek glory and name, second to covet heavy reward, third to fear punishment, fourth to avoid disaster and peril.
translations.idiomatic: From camp Xin Xiong memorialized: "Men face death in battle for fame, for reward, for fear of punishment, or to escape disaster—

sentences.zh: 非此數者，雖聖王不能使其臣，慈父不能厲其子矣。

translations.literal: Apart from these several, though a sage king cannot make his ministers act, a loving father cannot steel his sons.
translations.idiomatic: without these, neither sage king nor loving father can move them."

sentences.zh: 明主深知其情，故賞必行，罰必信，使親疏貴賤勇怯賢愚，聞鐘鼓之聲，見旌旗之列，莫不奮激，競赴敵場，豈懨久生而樂速死哉？

translations.literal: A clear ruler deeply knows their feelings; therefore rewards must be carried out, punishments must be believed, so that whether near or far, noble or base, brave or cowardly, worthy or foolish, hearing the sound of bells and drums and seeing ranks of banners, none do not strive in excitement and race to the enemy field—who would loathe long life and delight in swift death?
translations.idiomatic: A wise ruler knows this and makes rewards sure and punishments real, so all who hear the drums and see the banners rush to fight—not because they love death.

sentences.zh: 利害懸於前，欲罷不能耳。

translations.literal: Gain and harm hang before them; they wish to stop but cannot.
translations.idiomatic: Gain and loss stare them in the face; they cannot stand down.

sentences.zh: 自秦、隴逆節，蠻左亂常，已歷數載，凡在戎役數十萬人，扞御三方之師，敗多勝少，跡其所由，皆不明賞罰之故也。

translations.literal: From the time the Qin-Long rebels arose and the barbarian left disturbed the norms, already several years have passed; those in military service number several hundred thousand, holding off armies on three fronts—defeats many, victories few. Tracing the cause, all are from unclear rewards and punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Qin-Long rebels and southern tribes rose, years have passed and hundreds of thousands have served on three fronts, losing more than they win—all because rewards and punishments are unclear.

sentences.zh: 陛下雖降明詔，賞不移時，然將士之勳，歷稔不決，亡軍之卒，晏然在家，是使節士無所勸慕，庸人無所畏懾；

translations.literal: Your Majesty though has issued clear edicts that rewards are not delayed, yet officers' and soldiers' merit through years is not decided; soldiers of defeated armies sit at home in peace—this makes men of principle without whom to take example, and mediocre men without whom to fear;
translations.idiomatic: Your edicts promise swift reward, yet merit goes unpaid for years and men of broken armies sit safely at home—so the brave have no model and the timid no fear;

sentences.zh: 進而擊賊，死交而賞賒，退而逃散，身全而無罪，此其所以望敵奔沮，不肯盡力者也。

translations.literal: advancing to strike bandits, death in exchange for delayed reward; retreating to scatter, body whole and without crime—this is why they gaze at the enemy, break and slacken, and are unwilling to exert full strength.
translations.idiomatic: they die fighting for pay that never comes, while deserters go unpunished—so they hang back.

sentences.zh: 陛下誠能號令必信，賞罰必行，則軍威必張，盜賊必息矣。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty can truly make orders believed and rewards and punishments carried out, then military might will surely be displayed and bandits and robbers will surely cease."
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty makes command and punishment certain, the army will stand firm and the bandits fade."

sentences.zh: 」疏奏，不省。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted and not examined.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial went in and was ignored.

sentences.zh: 曹義宗等取魏順陽、馬圈，與裴衍等戰於淅陽，義宗等敗退。

translations.literal: Cao Yizong and others took Wei's Shunyang and Maquan, fought with Pei Yan and others at Xiyang; Yizong and the others were defeated and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Yizong took Shunyang and Maquan, fought Pei Yan at Xiyang, was beaten, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 衍等復取順陽，進圍馬圈。

translations.literal: Yan and the others again took Shunyang and advanced to besiege Maquan.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Yan's force retook Shunyang and pressed the siege of Maquan.

sentences.zh: 洛州刺史董紹以馬圈城堅，衍等糧少，上書言其必敗。

translations.literal: Governor of Luozhou Dong Shao, because Maquan city was strong and Yan and the others had little grain, submitted a memorial saying they were sure to be defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Shao, governor of Luozhou, wrote that Maquan was too strong and Pei Yan too short of food—he was bound to lose.

sentences.zh: 未幾，義宗擊衍等，破之，復取順陽。

translations.literal: Before long Yizong attacked Yan and the others, defeated them, and again took Shunyang.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Cao Yizong struck Pei Yan, routed him, and retook Shunyang.

sentences.zh: 魏以王羆為荊州刺史。

translations.literal: Wei appointed Wang Pi as Governor of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wei named Wang Pi governor of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 邵陵王綸攝南徐州事，在州喜怒不恆，肆行非法。

translations.literal: Prince of Shaoling Lun acted as administrator of Southern Xuzhou affairs; in the province his joy and anger were inconstant and he wantonly committed unlawful acts.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Lun of Shaoling held southern Xuzhou and ruled by whim, breaking the law at will.

sentences.zh: 遨遊市裡，問賣□旦者曰：「刺史何如？

translations.literal: Roaming the marketplace, he asked a seller of □dan, "How is the inspector?"
translations.idiomatic: Roaming the markets, he asked a vendor of □dan, "What do you think of the inspector?"

sentences.zh: 」對言：「躁虐。

translations.literal: " The reply was, "Fierce and cruel."
translations.idiomatic: " The man answered, "Cruel and violent."

sentences.zh: 」綸怒，令吞□旦而死。

translations.literal: " Lun in anger ordered him to swallow □dan and die.
translations.idiomatic: " Lun flew into a rage and made him swallow □dan until he died.

sentences.zh: 百姓惶駭，道路以目。

translations.literal: The common people were fearful and alarmed; on the roads they exchanged glances.
translations.idiomatic: The people were terrified; travelers only dared look at one another.

sentences.zh: 嘗逢喪車，奪孝子服而著之，匍匐號叫。

translations.literal: Once he met a funeral carriage, seized the filial son's mourning garments and put them on, and crawled and wailed.
translations.idiomatic: Once he met a funeral procession, snatched the mourner's hemp garments, put them on, and crawled wailing.

sentences.zh: 簽帥懼罪，密以聞。

translations.literal: The clerical commander feared guilt and secretly reported it.
translations.idiomatic: The chief clerk, fearing punishment, reported it in secret.

sentences.zh: 上始嚴責，綸不能改，於是遣代。

translations.literal: The Emperor at first sternly reproached him; Lun could not change, and thereupon he was replaced.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rebuked him sharply, but Lun would not mend his ways, and was recalled.

sentences.zh: 綸悖慢逾甚，乃取一老公短瘦類上者，加以袞冕，置之高坐，朝以為君，自陳無罪；

translations.literal: Lun's insolence grew ever worse. He took an old man short and thin who resembled the Emperor, added imperial robes and cap, set him on a high seat, paid court to him as sovereign, and declared himself innocent;
translations.idiomatic: Lun grew more defiant still. He found a short, thin old man who resembled the emperor, dressed him in imperial regalia, set him on a high seat, bowed to him as ruler, and proclaimed his own innocence;

sentences.zh: 使就坐剝褫，捶之於庭。

translations.literal: then had him stripped where he sat and beaten in the courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: then had the man stripped in the hall and beaten in the courtyard.

sentences.zh: 又作新棺，貯司馬崔會意，以□車輓歌為送葬之法，使嫗乘車悲號。

translations.literal: He also made a new coffin, shut in Marshal Cui Huiyi, used □cart and dirge-song as funeral custom, and had an old woman ride the cart wailing.
translations.idiomatic: He built a new coffin, shut Marshal Cui Huiyi inside, staged a mock funeral with a □cart and mourning songs, and set an old woman wailing on the cart.

sentences.zh: 會意不能堪，輕騎還都以聞。

translations.literal: Huiyi could not bear it; he rode lightly back to the capital to report.
translations.idiomatic: Huiyi could endure no more; he fled lightly on horseback to Jiankang to report it.

sentences.zh: 上恐其奔逸，以禁兵取之，將於獄賜盡，太子統流涕固諫，得免，戊子，免綸官，削爵土。

translations.literal: The Emperor feared he would flee; with palace guards he seized him and was about to grant him death in prison. Crown Prince Tong wept and firmly remonstrated and he was spared. On wuzi, Lun was removed from office and his fief and rank were stripped.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing flight, the emperor sent guards to seize him and ordered death in prison. Crown Prince Tong wept and pleaded until the sentence was lifted. On wuzi, Lun was dismissed and stripped of title and lands.

sentences.zh: 魏山胡劉蠡升反，自稱天子，置百官。

translations.literal: Shan-Hu of Wei Liu Lisheng rebelled, styled himself Son of Heaven, and appointed the hundred offices.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Lisheng of the Wei Shan-Hu rebelled, declared himself emperor, and set up a full bureaucracy.

sentences.zh: 初，敕勒酋長斛律金事懷朔鎮將楊鈞為軍主，行兵用匈奴法，望塵知馬步多少，嗅地知軍遠近。

translations.literal: Initially, Chile chieftain Helu Jin served Huaishuo Garrison commander Yang Jun as army commander; in marching he used Xiongnu methods—judging dust to know how many horse and foot, smelling earth to know an army's distance.
translations.idiomatic: Long ago the Chile chief Helu Jin served under Yang Jun, commander of Huaishuo Garrison, using Xiongnu scouting arts—reading dust for numbers of horse and foot, scenting earth for an army's distance.

sentences.zh: 及破六韓拔陵反，金擁眾歸之，拔陵署金為王。

translations.literal: When Poliuhan Baling rebelled, Jin led his multitude to join him; Baling appointed Jin king.
translations.idiomatic: When Poliuhan Baling rose, Jin brought his tribes to him and Baling made him king.

sentences.zh: 既而知拔陵終無所成，乃詣雲州降。

translations.literal: Having learned that Baling would in the end achieve nothing, he then went to Yunzhou to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing Baling would never prevail, he went to Yunzhou and submitted.

sentences.zh: 仍稍引其眾南出黃瓜堆，為杜洛周所破，脫身歸爾朱榮，榮以為別將。

translations.literal: Still he gradually led his multitude south out of Huangguadui; he was defeated by Du Luozhou, escaped with his body, returned to Erzhu Rong, and Rong made him a separate general.
translations.idiomatic: He then led his people south past Huangguadui, was broken by Du Luozhou, escaped to Erzhu Rong, and was made a detached general.
